About the St. Hubert's Animal Welfare Center

For over 80 years, St. Hubert’s Animal Welfare Center has been dedicated to helping animals in need and serving communities across New Jersey. With a people-focused, community-based approach, St. Hubert’s treats every animal as an individual and emphasizes specialized care for both animals and their families. Built on a foundation of rescue and adoption, St. Hubert’s operates extensive community programs, including access to veterinary care, pet food support, training services, and the nation’s leading pet transport initiative, WayStation. As part of the Humane Rescue Alliance, headquartered in Washington, D.C., St. Hubert’s is connected to the largest and most comprehensive animal services provider network in the region, impacting the lives of tens of thousands of animals each year.


Job Description

Like being in the know? Like talking to people, telling good stories, and making things happen online and out in the community?

As a Public Affairs Specialist at St. Huberts and the Humane Rescue Alliance, you’ll help shape how we show up in the world—from social media and digital storytelling to news coverage, community events, corporate partnerships, and conversations with local leaders.

Job Summary

A big part of your day-to-day work will be telling our stories on social media. You’ll help develop and create engaging content, manage day-to-day activity across our social channels, respond to, and interact with our online community, and look for opportunities to turn what’s happening across the organization into stories people want to see, share, and talk about. You’ll work closely with the Marketing team to keep our content fresh, timely, on-brand, and connected to what’s happening in our shelter and programs.

You’ll also help us build relationships and stay connected beyond our social channels. You might talk with a reporter about an animal in our care, coordinate a meeting with an elected official, work with a corporate partner on an activation, attend a community event, or help prepare a spokesperson for an interview. You’ll be someone who can move comfortably between writing a social post, answering a media request, planning an event, and talking with people in the community.

Reporting to the Director of Public Affairs, you’ll help make sure our voice is present, engaging, and consistent wherever people encounter us. We’re looking for someone who is curious, creative, organized, comfortable meeting new people, and able to spot a good story when they see one. If you enjoy variety, love social media, and want your work to connect people with animals and a mission you care about, this could be the role for you.


The Role: What You’ll Do

Media & Communications Support

  • Serve as a point of contact for routine media inquiries.
  • Draft press releases, media advisories, statements, and background materials.
  • Coordinate interviews and prepare briefing materials for organizational spokespeople.
  • Monitor media coverage and maintain tracking reports.
  • During Director absence, manage day-to-day media coordination with established escalation protocols for strategic or sensitive matters.

Government & Community Relations Support

  • Coordinate meetings and logistics with elected officials, community leaders, and key stakeholders.
  • Monitor local legislative and civic developments and flag relevant updates to leadership.
  • Assist in preparation of talking points, briefing materials, and stakeholder communications.
  • Support public affairs initiatives designed to advance HRA’s policy and community engagement priorities.

Digital Media 

  • Contribute to and execute integrated social media strategies, managing content creation and storytelling for HRA’s social media channels in alignment with organizational brand, communications, and engagement goals. 
  • Support Marketing Specialist in maintaining the content calendar.
  • Read, review, and respond to the community through social media channels.

Corporate Partnerships & Sponsorship Management

  • Manage and steward an assigned portfolio of corporate sponsors and business partners.
  • Identify and cultivate prospective corporate sponsors in coordination with the Director of Public Affairs and Development leadership.
  • Draft sponsorship proposals, agreements, and benefit summaries.
  • Ensure fulfillment of sponsor benefits, recognition, and reporting commitments.
  • Track corporate engagement activity and maintain accurate records in CRM systems.
  • Contribute to annual corporate revenue goals through strategic outreach, sponsor retention, and expansion of partnerships.

Events & Community Engagement

  • Lead coordination and logistical execution of external-facing events, corporate activations, and community engagement initiatives.
  • Manage sponsor activation, benefit fulfillment, and on-site representation at events.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to support successful execution of events and activations.
  • Be our representative at community gatherings, business forums, and civic meetings as delegated.

About You: Skills & Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience managing partnerships, sponsorships, or external engagement initiatives.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience drafting media and external materials.
  • Experience coordinating events or managing multi-stakeholder projects.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • Professional presence and confidence representing the organization in external settings.
  • Familiarity with CRM systems such as Raiser’s Edge preferred.
  • Commitment to our mission and values.

Qualifications – Education & Experience

  • 4–6 years of experience in communications, public affairs, nonprofit engagement, corporate relations, or related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, nonprofit management, political science, or related field preferred.
  • An equivalent combination of education and professional experience may be considered.

Where You'll Work: Physical Requirements & Work Environment

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

  • This position requires regular on-site presence at the Madison NJ campus and attendance at external events and meetings as necessary. 
  • Regularly sits at a computer station and operates electronic equipment.
  • Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends in support of events or media needs.
  • Ability to perform physical activity associated with event setup and coordination, including lifting, carrying, reaching, stooping, and standing for extended periods.
  • Comfortable working around cats, dogs, small animals, reptiles, fish, and wildlife.
  • Due to the nature of shelter work, may be exposed to deceased, fractious, or aggressive animals; common allergens; hostile or irate persons; zoonotic or other diseases; unpleasant noises, odors, or sights; and extreme temperatures.

Benefits Overview: Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA)

At the Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA), we are committed to supporting the well-being of our employees so they can continue making a meaningful impact for animals and the community. We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

Benefits include:

  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance: Multiple plan options available to meet individual and family needs 
  • Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA): Pre-tax options to help manage healthcare and dependent care expenses 
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Support: Administered through Empower, with tools and resources to help you plan for your future 
  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO): Including vacation, sick leave, and holidays to support rest and work-life balance 
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Confidential resources to support mental health, wellness, and life challenges 
  • Professional Development & Training Opportunities: Including Fear Free Certification and ongoing learning initiatives to support career growth 
  • Flexible Work Environment (Role-Dependent): Opportunities for hybrid or flexible scheduling based on position and operational needs 
  • Employee Discounts & Perks: Discounts on pet adoptions, veterinary products, and partner offerings 

Ready to Make an Impact? 


Apply today and become part of a team where your compassion, skills, and commitment will directly save lives and strengthen communities. 


The Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA) offers a comprehensive benefits package including healthcare, vision, dental and select offerings for pets. Additional information may be provided upon request. 

Multilingual candidates are encouraged to apply. A salary premium may be offered for multilingual candidates who demonstrate proficiency in written and oral testing.

 Location: Washington, D.C.
 Status: Full-Time, Exempt
 Reports To: Bobby Mann
 Like to talk on the phone? Prefer a coffee meeting to another Zoom call? Enjoy getting to know people—and hearing the stories behind why they care about animals?
 About the St. Hubert's Animal Welfare Center 
 For over 80 years, St. Hubert’s Animal Welfare Center has been dedicated to helping animals in need and serving communities across New Jersey. With a people-focused, community-based approach, St. Hubert’s treats every animal as an individual and emphasizes specialized care for both animals and their families. Built on a foundation of rescue and adoption, St. Hubert’s operates extensive community programs, including access to veterinary care, pet food support, training services, and the nation’s leading pet transport initiative, WayStation. As part of the Humane Rescue Alliance, headquartered in Washington, D.C., St. Hubert’s is connected to the largest and most comprehensive animal services provider network in the region, impacting the lives of tens of thousands of animals each year.
 Job Summary
 As a Development Officer at the Humane Rescue Alliance, you’ll spend your days building genuine relationships with people who want to make a difference for animals and the people who love them. You might meet a longtime donor for coffee and hear about their dog’s latest vet visit, give a prospective donor a tour of our campus, call a supporter to thank them for a recent gift, meet with a company about sponsoring an HRA event, or sit down with a donor to talk about making a larger gift.

 You’ll manage a portfolio of approximately 120–150 donors, corporate partners, and prospective supporters, getting to know what matters to them and finding meaningful ways for them to connect with HRA’s work. You’ll build relationships over time, make thoughtful asks, bring donors closer to our mission, and help turn their generosity into lifesaving care.

 This is a hands-on, relationship-driven fundraising role for someone who is naturally curious, organized, comfortable picking up the phone, and genuinely enjoys talking with people. You don’t have to have every conversation figured out in advance—you just need to know how to listen, build trust, follow through, and recognize when it’s time to ask.

 The Role: What You’ll Do
 Individual Giving & Portfolio Management
 Manage and grow a portfolio of approximately 120–150 individual donors, corporate partners, and qualified prospects.
 Develop personalized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies based on donor interests, capacity, and engagement.
 Conduct regular donor meetings, calls, campus tours, cultivation visits, and other meaningful relationship-building activities.
 Solicit significant philanthropic gifts and prepare written proposals or donor materials in partnership with internal teams when needed.
 Identify opportunities to retain, upgrade, and deepen relationships with existing donors.
 Qualify new prospects and build a strong pipeline of donors with the potential to increase their philanthropic support.
 Identify principal or transformational gift opportunities and partner with the Chief Advancement Officer and CEO on strategy and solicitation.
 Recognize potential planned giving opportunities and connect donors with appropriate resources when needed.
 Corporate Philanthropy
 Manage and grow assigned corporate philanthropic relationships.
 Build relationships with corporate decision-makers and solicit charitable gifts, sponsorships, matching gifts, and other philanthropic support.
 Secure sponsorships for major fundraising events and organizational initiatives.
 Partner with Public Affairs and other departments when volunteer activities or community engagement are part of a broader corporate relationship, while maintaining responsibility for the fundraising relationship.
 Stewardship & Collaboration
 Create personalized stewardship experiences that demonstrate the impact of donor support.
 Connect donors and prospects with HRA programs, staff, leadership, animals, and mission.
 Serve as the primary relationship manager for assigned donors participating in events and cultivation opportunities.
 Collaborate with Development Operations, Marketing and Communications, Public Affairs, program teams, and organizational leadership to advance donor relationships.
 Maintain accurate and timely donor records, strategies, contact reports, solicitations, and next steps in the fundraising database.
 Participate in regular portfolio reviews and use moves-management practices to advance donor relationships.
 About You: Skills & Qualifications
 Strong relationship-building, listening, communication, and interpersonal skills.
 Demonstrated ability to cultivate, solicit, and steward significant donor or client relationships.
 Ability to confidently make philanthropic asks and develop individualized relationship strategies.
 Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple relationships, priorities, and deadlines.
 Understanding of portfolio management, stewardship, moves management, and pipeline development.
 Ability to identify donor capacity, engagement, and readiness for solicitation.
 Experience with corporate philanthropy, sponsorships, or corporate relationship management strongly preferred.
 Familiarity with planned giving concepts preferred.
 Experience using fundraising databases or CRM systems such as Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce, DonorPerfect, or similar platforms.
 Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across departments.
 Passion for Humane Rescue Alliance’s mission.
 Qualifications – Education & Experience
 Five or more years of progressive experience in fundraising, development, donor relations, sales, or another relationship-based revenue role.
 Experience managing a portfolio of donors, prospects, clients, or other high-value relationships.
 Demonstrated success securing significant philanthropic gifts, preferably at the$5,000+ level.
 Bachelor’s degree preferred or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
 Experience in animal welfare or another mission-driven nonprofit environment preferred.
 Where You’ll Work: Physical Requirements & Work Environment
 This position is based at Humane Rescue Alliance’s Washington, D.C. campus and is designed to build philanthropic relationships throughout the Washington metropolitan region.
 This is a location-based, relationship-focused role. Regular onsite presence is required to host donor meetings and tours, participate in cultivation and stewardship opportunities, engage donors with programs and staff, and build a strong understanding of the organization’s work.
 After successful onboarding, demonstrated performance, and development of a strong understanding of the organization and portfolio, a hybrid work arrangement may be available based on organizational policy and the needs of the role. Regular onsite availability will remain required.
 Occasional evening and weekend work may be required.
 Limited regional travel may be required.
 Regular use of computer, phone, and office equipment.
 Must be comfortable working in proximity to cats, dogs, small animals, reptiles, fish, and wildlife.
 May be exposed to deceased, fractious, or aggressive animals; allergens; zoonotic diseases; unpleasant odors, noises, or sights.
 Ready to Make an Impact?
 Apply today and help build the philanthropic relationships that sustain HRA’s work for animals and the people who love them.
 Multilingual candidates are encouraged to apply. A salary premium may be offered for multilingual candidates who demonstrate proficiency in written and oral testing.
 HRA is committed to being an Equal Opportunity Employer and provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals requiring them.

description:
About the Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA) 

 For more than 150 years, the Humane Rescue Alliance has championed the protection of animals, support for people, and service to the community. With campuses in the District of Columbia and New Jersey, along with the nation’s leading pet transport initiative, it stands as the largest and most comprehensive animal services provider in the region. Each year, HRA transforms the lives of tens of thousands of animals through rescue and adoption, humane protection, access to medical care, innovative community programs, and legislative leadership. Its broad reach and deep expertise enable HRA to reimagine traditional sheltering and address the most complex challenges facing animals and the people who love them. 
 Job Summary 
 The Medical Administrative Assistant provides high-level administrative and client service support to the Humane Rescue Alliance’s fast-paced medical department. As a vital member of the team, this role ensures the smooth operation of daily workflows by delivering exceptional customer service, maintaining accuracy in documentation, and upholding a standard of efficiency and attention to detail in all interactions with clients, staff, and external partners. 

 This position requires at least one (1) year of prior experience as a veterinary receptionist or in a veterinary administrative support role. 
 The Role: What You’ll Do 
 Deliver exceptional customer service to all Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA) clients by warmly greeting visitors, maintaining a professional demeanor, and ensuring the cleanliness and welcoming appearance of the medical clinic reception area. 
 Respond promptly and courteously to inquiries via phone and email from HRA departments, fosters, and members of the public. 
 Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Medical Department, including but not limited to: Scheduling exams and surgeries for in-shelter animals, foster pets, and public clients. 
 Preparing, updating, and maintaining accurate and complete medical records (e.g., exams, surgeries, medications) using Clinic HQ and PetPoint systems. 
 Filling medications and coordinating prescription requests with external pharmacies. 
 Assisting with patient intake and discharge, including providing client education and support. 
 Communicating with fosters, pet owners, and internal staff to coordinate exam and treatment needs. 

 Support volunteer integration by actively participating in their onboarding, training, safety, engagement, and performance oversight to ensure a positive and productive experience. 
 Handle complex customer service situations involving ill or injured animals or denials of service with empathy and professionalism. 
 Demonstrate sound judgment in addressing client concerns, escalating issues to supervisors or coordinating with other departments as needed. 
 Represent HRA in a consistently professional, respectful, and courteous manner when interacting with the public, colleagues, and volunteers. 
 Provide support for general shelter operations when needed, including customer care and animal care duties. 
 Participate in on-site and off-site medical events, including planning, transporting animals (driving HRA vehicles as needed), and overseeing animals and volunteers during events. 
 Assist with inventory tracking and management for all medical programs and supplies. 
 Adhere to all safety protocols to maintain a safe and healthy environment for people and animals. Promptly report and address any safety concerns or violations. 
 Attend and participate in medical department meetings, rounds, and training sessions as assigned. 
 About You: Skills & Qualifications 
 The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to 
 perform essential functions. 
 Regularly sits at a computer station and operates electronic equipment. 
 Ability to lift 50 pounds unassisted regularly, 50+ pounds assisted. 
 Ability to be comfortable working with cats, dogs, small animals, reptiles, fish, and wildlife. 
 Ability to be comfortable working in a medical environment, with the associated sights, sounds, and smells. 
 Ability to perform strenuous physical activity daily, including but not limited to lifting and carrying, reaching, stooping, squatting, and bending. Regularly moves about the facilities to coordinate work. Typically stands, bends, stoops, and crouches while working special events. 
 Due to the nature of shelter work, may be exposed to deceased, fractious, or aggressive animals; common allergens; hostile or irate persons; zoonotic or other diseases; unpleasant noises, odors, or sights; and extreme temperatures. 
 Knowledge of or ability to learn medical and shelter terminology. 
 Knowledge of or ability to learn animal shelter procedures and protocols. 
 Ability to routinely work evenings, weekends, and holidays as scheduled. 
 Work collaboratively and with confidence in a high-stress, fast-paced work environment. Ability to work effectively, both independently and in a team environment, in an atmosphere of multiple projects, shifting priorities, and deadline pressures. Ability to be flexible, detail-oriented, and able to prioritize. 
 Ability to perform basic math and think critically. 
 Excellent interpersonal skills with a customer-service orientation. Ability to communicate in a friendly and professional manner with a variety of individuals representing the public, board members, volunteers, donors, and employees. Ability to conduct and handle difficult conversations. 
 Computer literacy with proficient use of programs including Microsoft Office programs and email, database management software, and payment processing. Familiarity with shelter or veterinary practice software is highly desired; experience specifically with veterinary practice management and shelter software is a plus. 
 Passion for the Humane Rescue Alliance mission, for caring for all animals regardless of age, breed, temperament, or species, and supporting and educating members of the public, free of judgment or bias. 
 Ability to manage the emotional aspect of work in an animal shelter environment in a positive professional manner. 
 Qualifications – Education & Experience 
 At least one (1) year of experience in a veterinary setting (clinic, hospital, or shelter) required; additional experience or transferable skills are highly valued. 
 Strong customer service and communication skills , with the ability to remain calm, compassionate, and professional in emotionally charged situations. 
 Proficiency with computer systems , including MS 365, payment processing, and veterinary practice management software (Clinic HQ or PetPoint experience a plus ). 
 Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail , with the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. 
 Knowledge of or ability to learn animal shelter procedures, protocols, and commonly prescribed veterinary medications; able to clearly communicate medication instructions to clients. 
 Ability to engage respectfully and effectively with a diverse range of individuals including clients, volunteers, donors, board members, and colleagues, and to navigate challenging conversations with professionalism. 
 Willingness to work a flexible schedule , including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed. 
 Resilience and emotional maturity to manage the demands of an animal shelter environment with a positive, team-oriented attitude. 
 Commitment to the mission and values of the Humane Rescue Alliance—providing compassionate care and support for all animals and the people who love them. 
 High school diploma, GED, or equivalent experience demonstrating the knowledge and skills required for the role. 
 Prior experience in an animal shelter or veterinary clinic preferred. 
 Where You’ll Work: 

 This position is primarily based at our MLK Avenue campus in Washington, D.C., with occasional work at our Oglethorpe Street campus as needed. Team members may also be asked to support community events, vaccine clinics, adoption fairs, and outreach programs throughout the District. About the Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA)


For more than 150 years, the Humane Rescue Alliance has championed the protection of animals, support for people, and service to the community. With campuses in the District of Columbia and New Jersey, along with the nation’s leading pet transport initiative, it stands as the largest and most comprehensive animal services provider in the region. Each year, HRA transforms the lives of tens of thousands of animals through rescue and adoption, humane protection, access to medical care, innovative community programs, and legislative leadership. Its broad reach and deep expertise enable HRA to reimagine traditional sheltering and address the most complex challenges facing animals and the people who love them.    

Job Summary

The Medical Administrative Assistant provides high-level administrative and client service support to the Humane Rescue Alliance’s fast-paced medical department. As a vital member of the team, this role ensures the smooth operation of daily workflows by delivering exceptional customer service, maintaining accuracy in documentation, and upholding a standard of efficiency and attention to detail in all interactions with clients, staff, and external partners.  


This position requires at least one (1) year of prior experience as a veterinary receptionist or in a veterinary administrative support role.

The Role: What You’ll Do

  • Deliver exceptional customer service to all Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA) clients by warmly greeting visitors, maintaining a professional demeanor, and ensuring the cleanliness and welcoming appearance of the medical clinic reception area.
  • Respond promptly and courteously to inquiries via phone and email from HRA departments, fosters, and members of the public.
  • Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Medical Department, including but not limited to:
    • Scheduling exams and surgeries for in-shelter animals, foster pets, and public clients.
    • Preparing, updating, and maintaining accurate and complete medical records (e.g., exams, surgeries, medications) using Clinic HQ and PetPoint systems.
    • Filling medications and coordinating prescription requests with external pharmacies.
    • Assisting with patient intake and discharge, including providing client education and support.
    • Communicating with fosters, pet owners, and internal staff to coordinate exam and treatment needs.
  • Support volunteer integration by actively participating in their onboarding, training, safety, engagement, and performance oversight to ensure a positive and productive experience.
  • Handle complex customer service situations involving ill or injured animals or denials of service with empathy and professionalism.
  • Demonstrate sound judgment in addressing client concerns, escalating issues to supervisors or coordinating with other departments as needed.
  • Represent HRA in a consistently professional, respectful, and courteous manner when interacting with the public, colleagues, and volunteers.
  • Provide support for general shelter operations when needed, including customer care and animal care duties.
  • Participate in on-site and off-site medical events, including planning, transporting animals (driving HRA vehicles as needed), and overseeing animals and volunteers during events.
  • Assist with inventory tracking and management for all medical programs and supplies.
  • Adhere to all safety protocols to maintain a safe and healthy environment for people and animals. Promptly report and address any safety concerns or violations.
  • Attend and participate in medical department meetings, rounds, and training sessions as assigned. 

About You: Skills & Qualifications

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to  

perform essential functions. 

  • Regularly sits at a computer station and operates electronic equipment.
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds unassisted regularly, 50+ pounds assisted.
  • Ability to be comfortable working with cats, dogs, small animals, reptiles, fish, and wildlife.
  • Ability to be comfortable working in a medical environment, with the associated sights, sounds, and smells. 
  • Ability to perform strenuous physical activity daily, including but not limited to lifting and carrying, reaching, stooping, squatting, and bending. Regularly moves about the facilities to coordinate work. Typically stands, bends, stoops, and crouches while working special events.
  • Due to the nature of shelter work, may be exposed to deceased, fractious, or aggressive animals; common allergens; hostile or irate persons; zoonotic or other diseases; unpleasant noises, odors, or sights; and extreme temperatures.
  • Knowledge of or ability to learn medical and shelter terminology. 
  • Knowledge of or ability to learn animal shelter procedures and protocols. 
  • Ability to routinely work evenings, weekends, and holidays as scheduled. 
  • Work collaboratively and with confidence in a high-stress, fast-paced work environment. Ability to work effectively, both independently and in a team environment, in an atmosphere of multiple projects, shifting priorities, and deadline pressures. Ability to be flexible, detail-oriented, and able to prioritize. 
  • Ability to perform basic math and think critically.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with a customer-service orientation. Ability to communicate in a friendly and professional manner with a variety of individuals representing the public, board members, volunteers, donors, and employees. Ability to conduct and handle difficult conversations. 
  • Computer literacy with proficient use of programs including Microsoft Office programs and email, database management software, and payment processing. Familiarity with shelter or veterinary practice software is highly desired; experience specifically with veterinary practice management and shelter software is a plus. 
  • Passion for the Humane Rescue Alliance mission, for caring for all animals regardless of age, breed, temperament, or species, and supporting and educating members of the public, free of judgment or bias. 
  • Ability to manage the emotional aspect of work in an animal shelter environment in a positive professional manner.

Qualifications – Education & Experience

  • At least one (1) year of experience in a veterinary setting (clinic, hospital, or shelter) required; additional experience or transferable skills are highly valued.
  • Strong customer service and communication skills, with the ability to remain calm, compassionate, and professional in emotionally charged situations.
  • Proficiency with computer systems, including MS 365, payment processing, and veterinary practice management software (Clinic HQ or PetPoint experience a plus).
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment.
  • Knowledge of or ability to learn animal shelter procedures, protocols, and commonly prescribed veterinary medications; able to clearly communicate medication instructions to clients.
  • Ability to engage respectfully and effectively with a diverse range of individuals including clients, volunteers, donors, board members, and colleagues, and to navigate challenging conversations with professionalism.
  • Willingness to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.
  • Resilience and emotional maturity to manage the demands of an animal shelter environment with a positive, team-oriented attitude.
  • Commitment to the mission and values of the Humane Rescue Alliance—providing compassionate care and support for all animals and the people who love them.
  • High school diploma, GED, or equivalent experience demonstrating the knowledge and skills required for the role.
  • Prior experience in an animal shelter or veterinary clinic preferred.

Where You’ll Work:

This position is primarily based at our MLK Avenue campus in Washington, D.C., with occasional work at our Oglethorpe Street campus as needed. Team members may also be asked to support community events, vaccine clinics, adoption fairs, and outreach programs throughout the District. All approved off-site work is considered part of your paid time. Working at HRA means being part of a compassionate, hands-on environment where every day is different. Team members in this role should be prepared for the following:

  • Must be comfortable working with dogs, cats, small animals, reptiles, fish, and wildlife.
  • Requires daily movement including bending, lifting, standing, walking, and animal handling.
  • Regular exposure to sick, injured, aggressive, or deceased animals, as well as strong odors or noises.
  • Ability to remain calm, compassionate, and professional in emotional or stressful situations.
  • Must be available to work weekends, evenings, holidays, and overtime as needed.

The Humane Rescue Alliance (HRA) offers a comprehensive benefits package including healthcare, vision, dental and select offerings for pets.  Additional information may be provided upon request.

Multilingual candidates are encouraged to apply. A salary premium may be offered for multilingual candidates who demonstrate proficiency in written and oral testing. 

 HRA is committed to being an Equal Opportunity Employer, and does not discriminate because of race, color, creed, gender, religion, national origin, disability, age, pregnancy, genetic predisposition or carrier status, marital status, citizenship status, or sexual orientation. Accommodations will be provided to qualified individuals requiring them.

 Ability to be comfortable working with dogs.
 Ability to perform strenuous physical activity daily, including but not limited to lifting and carrying, reaching, stooping, squatting, and bending.

 Work with outside vendors (Direct Answer, Donor Advised Funds, workplace giving confirmations, etc.)
 Notify team members of special handling and other important giving
 Provide admin support to DDO and CAO when requested
 Schedule and coordinate volunteers to assist with Devo ack mailing and special projects
 Assist Development Dept on a case-by-case basis 
 Other duties as assigned
 Phone Inquiries 
 Respond to inquiries from supporters and potential supporters within 4 business hours
 Always maintain a high standard of customer service
 Flag small event inquiries and share with the events team 
 Direct inquiries not related to Development appropriate HRA staff person or department
 Events Support 
 Support Events team if they need help preparing materials for a large event
 Assist with large HRA annual events (evening or weekends may be required – once or twice a year)
 Donor Communications 
 Generate and process donor acknowledgement letters
 Send birthday, thank you, other specialized cards upon request
 Assist with YE ack letter processing
 Create customized thank you letters for DDO, CAO and major gifts team
 Perform thank you calls 
 Manage the developme nt team's email box
 Call monthly donors for payment updates
 Process and send tribute gift notification cards and acknowledgements
 Answer general inquiries from donors/the community
 Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor

 Excellent organizational and communication skills 
 Meticulous attention to detail
 Ability to research donor information for accurate record keeping
 CRM Database experience (Raiser’s Edge NXT and Luminate) 
 Proficient in Microsoft Office applications including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Advanced Word and Excel skills preferred
 Self-starter with the ability to multi-task, work independently, and as part of a team.
 Basic knowledge of fundraising and donor gift processing
 Creative thinker who can contribute to gift processing time saving ideas and efficiencies
 Excellent verbal communication, interpersonal and relationship-building skills to effectively work with a variety of people and personalities
 Proven ability to collaborate with colleagues, donors, and volunteers
 Ability to present, inform and motivate individuals and groups about HRA’s mission and the importance of raising funds in support of the mission
 Understands the confidential nature of donor information and compliance protocol
 Represent HRA in a professional, informed manner
 Ability to troubleshoot software issues and reach out to them for further help if necessary
 Proven ability to manage workflow and meet deadlines
 Excellent time management and calendar management skills
 Ability to work independently and research answers to questions once given a specified task
 Ability to show up on time and adhere to the assigned work hours
 Qualifications – Education & Experience 
 College degree or equivalent combination of education and experience
 Minimum one year of administrative office experience, preferably in a non-profit environment
 Customer Service and Donor Services experience preferred
 Minimum two years CRM Database experience (Raiser’s Edge NXT and Luminate preferred) 
 Where You'll Work: Physical Requirements & Work Environment 
 The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. 
 Regularly sits at a computer station and operates electronic equipment 
 Frequently lifts objects weighing up to 30 pounds when moving supplies and managing special events 
 Typically stands, bends, stoops and crouches while working special events 
 Regularly moves about the facility to coordinate work 
 Occasional weekend and evening work (a few times a year)

 Commuter Benefits (WMATA SmartBenefits): Pre-tax transit benefits for metro, bus, and eligible commuting expenses 
 Professional Development & Training Opportunities: Including Fear Free Certification and ongoing learning initiatives to support career growth
 Flexible Work Environment (Role-Dependent): Opportunities for hybrid or flexible scheduling based on position and operational needs 
 Employee Discounts & Perks: Discounts on pet adoptions, veterinary products, and partner offerings 
 Ready to Make an Impact? 

 Apply today and become part of a team where your compassion, skills, and commitment will directly save lives and strengthen communities.

 contractors, residential cleaners, and more.
 The Junior Account Executive is a developmental sales role focused on supporting revenue growth, member engagement, account
 development, and customer retention across assigned accounts and prospects. This position will work closely with Account
 Executives and the Membership Engagement team to identify opportunities, build customer relationships, and develop the skills
 necessary to progress into an Account Executive role.
 The Junior Account Executive will assist throughout the sales process, including prospecting, lead qualification, customer follow-up,
 proposal development, closing smaller opportunities, and supporting the growth of existing accounts. The position will also help
 identify opportunities for membership, education, certification, sponsorships, media and advertising, events, and other ISSA products
 and services.
 This role is designed to provide hands-on experience in consultative selling, relationship management, and pipeline development
 while learning ISSA’s products, services, and the cleaning and facility solutions industry. With demonstrated performance and
 continued development, the Junior Account Executive is expected to progress toward the responsibilities and performance
 expectations of an Account Executive.
 Duties and Responsibilities 
 • Supports revenue generation for new membership and non-dues revenue, including education, certification, sponsorships, media
 & advertising, signature initiatives, event attendance, and renewals.
 • Prospect, nurture, qualify, and follow up with leads.
 • Assist Account Executives with assigned accounts and sales opportunities.
 • Develop and maintain relationships with current and prospective members.
 • Identify opportunities to expand member engagement and introduce customers to relevant ISSA products and services.
 • Assist with new membership onboarding and customer follow-up.
 • Conduct outbound calls, emails, and other prospecting activities to generate new opportunities.
 • Maintain accurate customer and opportunity information within Salesforce.
 • Schedule and participate in customer calls and meetings as appropriate.
 • Prepare and assist with proposals, quotes, and other sales materials.
 • Follow up on open opportunities and help move prospects through the sales process.

 products and services.

 Account Executive responsibilities.

 Key Competencies 
 • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
 • Customer-focused with the ability to build positive relationships.
 • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
 • Willingness to learn and develop sales skills.
 • Ability to multitask and work efficiently under deadlines.
 • Comfortable making outbound calls and engaging with prospective customers.
 • Positive, professional, and team-oriented attitude.
 • Ability to work independently while also collaborating with the sales team.
 • Basic understanding of sales and customer service principles.
 • Ability to utilize Salesforce and other technology to track customer interactions and sales activity.
 Key Performance Indicators 
 Final key performance indicators (KPI’s) will be established based on member segmentation and the individual’s level of development
 by your direct supervisor.
 • New Revenue Generated
 • Number of Qualified Opportunities Created
 • Close Percentage
 • Average Sale Size
 • Outbound Sales Activity
 • Member/Customer Engagement
 • Pipeline Development
 Mandatory Qualifications 
 • Demonstrated interest in developing a career in sales, account management, or customer engagement.
 • Ability to work within an office setting.
 • Proficient in CRM and/or AMS software or ability to learn quickly.
 • Associate degree in business administration or equivalent work experience preferred.
 • 1–2 years of experience in sales, customer service, account management, business development, or a related field preferred.
 • Proficient in Microsoft Office suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams.
 Beneficial Qualifications 
 • Experience working with trade associations or a similar not-for-profit environment a plus.
 • Knowledge of the cleaning, facilities management, and/or restoration industry a plus.
 • Experience with Salesforce a plus.
 • Previous experience in a membership-based organization a plus.
 • Project management experience or certification a plus.

We all face challenges and transitions in our lives, and when we do, we must be able to count on the strength of community for support. For the people of Los Angeles, Jewish Family Service LA (JFSLA) is that trusted source of support. We are a comprehensive network of services that welcomes individuals and families of all ages and identities to our full spectrum of care. Our highly trained staff and volunteers work closely with individuals and their loved ones to problem-solve and guide them on their paths to safety, security, wellness, and fulfillment. 
 JFSLA staff share in our mission and work towards our goals with the highest level of responsibility, professionalism, and integrity. JFS demonstrates our commitment to our staff by offering a comprehensive benefits package and a nurturing environment. 
 JFSLA is committed to cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and connectedness. In recruiting for our team, we seek the unique contributions that individuals can bring from all backgrounds. We strive for a diverse team in order to better serve our clients and ensure our excellence as an organization in identifying, designing and delivering solutions. 

 Be part of our commitment and join our family. For more information on our philosophy and services, please tour our website www.jfsla.org 

 The Social Work I is responsible for conducting in-depth intakes and assessments covering psychological, social and physical, and environmental concerns for frail, elderly clients; Holocaust survivors and their families. S/he will evaluate clients, identify the potential limitations which impede independent living and activate resources to allow client to remain safely in the home setting. 

 QUALIFICATIONS : 

 Bachelors degree in social work or a related field 
 Current unrestricted CA Driver’s License and proof of auto insurance 
 Bilingual Russian/Spanish preferred 
 Experience and interest in providing care to older persons required 
 Care management and community-based service delivery experience required 
 Knowledge of community resources and the aging process 
 Experience working with seniors, caregivers and mentally disabled clients 
 Knowledge of safety issues when working with at-risk clients 
 Experience conducting in-home visit strongly preferred 
 Must be computer literate in MS Office applications (Word, Excel and Outlook) 
 Candidates must have interest and demonstrated ability to: Work in an interdisciplinary community setting 
 Be culturally sensitive, able to work with a multicultural client population 
 Work in a non-judgmental manner and work as part of a team 
 Maintain professional boundaries 
 Exercise sound casework judgment and fiscal management skills 
 Comply with documentation procedures 

 Must pass a criminal background check (Live Scan fingerprinting) prior to beginning employment 
 RESPONSIBILITIES/ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS : 

 Conducts in-depth intakes and assessment covering psychological, social, physical, and environmental concerns for clients that are survivors of the Holocaust 
 Develops a comprehensive care plan including all social services needed by the client 
 Coordinates the delivery of all services in the care plan 
 Responds to intake callers and follows up on client situation as needed 
 Reviews and authorizes services every month 
 Offers crisis intervention 
 Provides outreach and support per funding source requirements 
 Prepares quarterly reports for the funding sources (Report include statistics on intake and outreach, number of clients serve, description of services, expenditures for each client served through grant) 
 Provides short-term or ongoing psychotherapeutic support to low income Holocaust survivors and their families as needed 
 Identifies and develops family and other informal support systems for the client 
 Refer clients to specialist consultants to provide additional detailed evaluation and recommendations for improvement of the client’s functional level 
 Prepares case recording, maintenance of financial records; and reporting on a timely and relevant basis 
 Provide timely documentation and oversee chart record keeping per funding requirements. 
 Selects, negotiates and budgets supportive services for clients 
 May be required to be a Field Work Supervisor and/ or preceptor for Social Work students 
 Other related duties as assigned 
 Hours towards licensure available but not guaranteed 
 Jewish Family Service is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

 Job Description
 Aerospace Estimation Engineer – Composite Structures & Honeycomb Products
 Location: Pottsville, Pennsylvania, USA (Initial Onsite Visit Required; Primarily Remote Thereafter)
 Position Overview 
 We are seeking an experienced Aerospace Estimation Engineer with hands-on experience in composite structures, honeycomb core products, aerospace manufacturing processes, and cost estimation/quoting activities within commercial and defense aerospace sectors to support engineering estimating and quotation activities for a leading aerospace composites manufacturer based in Pottsville, PA. The role will support bidding, proposal development, cost estimation, and manufacturing assessments across a diverse portfolio including – Commercial, Defense and Emerging Aviation platforms
 The successful candidate will work closely with the client's Engineering Manager and cross-functional manufacturing teams to develop accurate labor, material, tooling, and manufacturing cost estimates for composite and honeycomb-based products.
 Industry Experience 
 Minimum 5 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, cost estimation, bid engineering, or quotation development.
 Hands-on experience with aerospace composite structures, honeycomb core products, prepreg materials, or advanced manufacturing environments.
 Familiarity with commercial and defense aerospace program requirements, quality standards, and compliance expectations.
 Proven ability to develop estimates covering labor, materials, tooling, machine utilization, process time, and manufacturing overhead.
 Strong knowledge of composite manufacturing processes, including prepreg handling, layup, tooling, curing, trimming, machining, forming, and assembly.
 Experience assessing honeycomb core forming, shaping, machining, fabrication, and production routing methods.

 Technical Skills:
 Strong understanding of composite structures, honeycomb core products, prepreg materials, and aerospace manufacturing processes.
 Proficiency in interpreting RFQs, engineering drawings, specifications, bills of material, and manufacturing requirements.
 Practical knowledge of core forming, layup, curing, machining, trimming, fabrication, assembly, and inspection processes.
 Experience developing labor, material, tooling, machine, and overhead cost estimates for aerospace products.
 Working familiarity with NC programming concepts, manufacturing routings, tooling, process planning, and resource loading.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify cost drivers, production risks, and manufacturability constraints.
 Effective communication and stakeholder collaboration skills across engineering, manufacturing, operations, supply chain, and business teams.
 Ability to standardize estimating assumptions, templates, methods, and lessons learned to improve quote quality and turnaround time.

 Key Responsibilities: Summary of Responsibilities & Skills
 Analyze customer RFQs, engineering drawings, specifications, and technical requirements to develop accurate engineering quotations.
 Interpret technical requirements and manufacturing considerations for aerospace composites, honeycomb, commercial, defense, space, and emerging aviation programs.
 Review production methods, manufacturing routings, and process plans for composite and honeycomb structures.
 Assess fabrication, machining, core forming, trimming, assembly, and other manufacturing operations to identify key cost drivers and manufacturability considerations.
 Apply aerospace cost-estimation principles and manufacturing cost-modeling methodologies to quotation activities.
 Estimate labor requirements, process cycle times, tooling needs, machine utilization, and manufacturing resources required for production.
 Develop detailed cost models covering material, labor, tooling, machine utilization, and manufacturing overheads.
 Prepare cost estimates and engineering quotations for aerospace composite products and assemblies.
 Support proposal preparation, bid reviews, and quotation submissions for commercial and defense aerospace opportunities.
 Participate in technical reviews, customer proposal discussions, and cross-functional decision-making activities.
 Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, operations, and business teams to improve estimating accuracy, consistency, and responsiveness.
 Leverage knowledge of NC programming concepts, tooling, process planning, and aerospace manufacturing operations to enhance estimate quality and manufacturability assessments.
 Establish scalable estimating methodologies, standards, templates, and best practices to support future growth and operational efficiency.

 Job Description
 MRB Engineer – Composite Manufacturing & Production Support
 Location: Kent, WA, USA 
 Position Overview 
 We are seeking an experienced MRB (Material Review Board) Engineer to support our customer who is in composite manufacturing operations. The role will support production teams in the disposition of non-conformances, development of MRB decisions, root cause and corrective action (RCCA) investigations, and continuous improvement initiatives across aerospace composite and honeycomb manufacturing operations.
 The ideal candidate will have strong shop floor experience working directly with production, quality, manufacturing engineering, and operations teams in a fast-paced aerospace manufacturing environment. This individual will provide engineering disposition support, author MRB tags, perform failure investigations, identify systemic issues, and generate actionable insights to improve quality, producibility, and manufacturing performance.

 Industry Experience
 Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
 Minimum 5–10 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing, production engineering, MRB, liaison engineering, quality engineering, or manufacturing engineering.
 Hands-on experience supporting aerospace production environments involving composites, honeycomb structures, bonded assemblies, machined parts, sheet metal components, or advanced composite materials.
 Strong shop floor experience working directly with operators, inspectors, quality engineers, manufacturing engineers, and production leadership.
 Experience reviewing and dispositioning production non-conformances within aerospace manufacturing environments.
 Experience conducting Root Cause Corrective Action (RCCA), failure investigations, and production problem resolution.
 Familiarity with commercial and defense aerospace manufacturing standards, quality requirements, and regulatory compliance.
 Experience supporting continuous improvement initiatives focused on defect reduction, process capability improvement, and manufacturing excellence.
 Prior OEM, Tier-1 supplier, aerospace structures, composites, or advanced manufacturing experience preferred.
 MRB delegation or prior experience supporting OEM MRB processes (e.g., Boeing, Airbus, Spirit, Collins, etc.) is highly desirable.

 Key Responsibilities: 
 Review, analyze, and disposition manufacturing non-conformances through the Material Review Board (MRB) process.
 Prepare, document, and release MRB tags and engineering dispositions in accordance with customer, regulatory, and internal quality requirements.
 Provide engineering support to production teams for composite, honeycomb, bonded, machined, and assembled aerospace products.
 Perform technical evaluations of discrepant hardware and determine appropriate repair, rework, use-as-is, or scrap dispositions.
 Investigate recurring quality issues and non-conformances to identify root causes and systemic process gaps.
 Lead and support RCCA activities using structured problem-solving methodologies such as 5-Why, Fishbone, Pareto, and related analytical techniques.
 Collaborate with Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Production, and Supplier Quality teams to implement effective corrective and preventive actions.
 Analyze production data and quality trends to generate insights and recommendations for defect reduction and process improvement.
 Support containment activities, concession reviews, and customer-driven quality investigations.
 Participate in shop floor troubleshooting and provide rapid engineering support to minimize production disruptions.
 Review engineering drawings, specifications, manufacturing plans, and process documentation to support MRB decision-making.
 Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on producibility, quality performance, and manufacturing efficiency.
 Participate in cross-functional review boards and communicate technical recommendations to stakeholders and management.

 Technical Skills & Core Competencies
 Strong knowledge of aerospace MRB processes, non-conformance dispositioning, and engineering release practices.
 Experience writing and approving MRB tags, discrepancy reports, concession requests, and engineering dispositions.
 Strong RCCA and problem-solving skills with experience applying structured root cause methodologies.
 Working knowledge of aerospace manufacturing processes including composite layup, curing, bonding, honeycomb fabrication, machining, trimming, assembly, and inspection.
 Ability to interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, material specifications, process specifications, and manufacturing plans.
 Familiarity with aerospace quality systems, AS9100 requirements, and production quality controls.
 Experience using quality and engineering systems for defect tracking, investigation, and corrective action management.
 Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify trends, develop insights, and recommend sustainable process improvements.
 Effective communication skills with the ability to work directly with shop floor personnel, engineering teams, quality organizations, and leadership.
 Experience participating in cross-functional investigations and driving closure of corrective actions.

IT Infrastructure Manager 
 The IT Infrastructure Manager leads the strategy, reliability, security, and lifecycle management of enterprise infrastructure across Kalmbach Feeds. The role is accountable for on-premises and emerging cloud platforms, networks, servers, storage, telecommunications, databases, backup, recovery, and related services supporting offices, manufacturing plants, and other company locations. The manager leads the infrastructure team and strategic partners, maintains a multi-year roadmap, supports operating and capital budget development, manages spending within approved budgets, and ensures infrastructure remains reliable, resilient, secure, recoverable, and scalable as the business grows.

 The Role: 
 Lead and develop the infrastructure team; set clear ownership, priorities, performance expectations, and technical standards.
 Build a culture of reliable execution by setting realistic commitments, assigning clear owners and deadlines, tracking progress, addressing barriers early, and holding the team accountable for results. Communicate risks or delays promptly and provide recovery plans.
 Ensure infrastructure is reliable, resilient, secure, and recoverable to support continuous business and production operations.
 Set monitoring, alerting, capacity, and performance standards. Use service trends to identify risk, prevent recurring issues, and meet availability targets.
 Deliver infrastructure for new plants, warehouses, offices, and expansions, aligning design, procurement, installation, testing, and readiness with construction and growth schedules.
 Partner with Service Desk, Business Systems, Analytics, and Cybersecurity leaders to define requirements, resolve cross-functional issues, and ensure reliable business services.
 Evaluate technology trends and recommend improvements aligned with business objectives, operational performance, and risk reduction.
 Maintain multi-year infrastructure roadmaps; lead approved initiatives, manage risks and dependencies, and communicate progress, decisions, costs, and lifecycle needs.
 Support budget development with forecasts, lifecycle plans, estimates, and vendor input. Manage contracts, vendors, and spending within approved budgets; report service, risk, project, vendor, and financial performance.
 Define and execute a scalable hybrid-cloud strategy, including hosting, architecture, security, capacity, cost, and lifecycle standards. Translate business demand and resilience needs into timely infrastructure investments.
 Enforce patching, maintenance, configuration, documentation, and lifecycle standards to keep infrastructure secure, supportable, licensed, and minimally disruptive to operations.
 Own backup, recovery, and disaster-recovery strategies. Define recovery objectives, verify backups, test recovery, remediate gaps, and report readiness and risk.
 Partner with Cybersecurity to implement infrastructure controls, remediate vulnerabilities, and strengthen privileged access, configuration, logging, segmentation, and incident response. Document and communicate risks and exceptions.
 Lead infrastructure escalations, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions. Maintain support documentation and enable the Service Desk to resolve issues at the lowest appropriate level.

 Skills and Experience: 
 Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
 10 or more years of progressively responsible infrastructure or IT operations experience, including at least 5 years leading technical teams, enterprise platforms, service providers, or major initiatives in a multi-site environment.
 Demonstrated experience leading enterprise networks, compute, virtualization, storage, telecommunications, databases, monitoring, backup, recovery, and related infrastructure services. Experience with VMware, SolarWinds, Microsoft SQL Server, or comparable enterprise platforms is preferred.
 Demonstrated experience designing, governing, and operating hybrid-cloud environments, including cloud and on-premises integration, networking, security, monitoring, cost management, capacity planning, and technology lifecycle management. Microsoft Azure experience is strongly preferred.
 Experience supporting infrastructure in a multi-site manufacturing, distribution, or similarly availability-sensitive environment, including delivery of technology for new plants, warehouses, offices, or major site expansions.
 Demonstrated ability to set direction, establish accountability, coach and develop employees, delegate effectively, manage performance, and build a collaborative, high-performing technical team.
 Experience managing vendors, contracts, licensing, professional services, and managed-service providers, including service reviews, performance escalation, cost control, renewal planning, and operating and capital budget input.
 Demonstrated ability to balance operational support, cybersecurity remediation, lifecycle maintenance, project delivery, construction-driven deadlines, and unplanned incidents while making clear resource and priority decisions.
 Demonstrated ability to maintain portfolio visibility, enforce change discipline, and ensure priority or commitment changes are communicated, aligned, and approved before resources are redirected.
 Working knowledge of infrastructure security practices, including vulnerability remediation, privileged access, secure configuration, logging, network segmentation, patch governance, and incident response.
 Experience establishing and using service and operational measures such as availability, incident trends, capacity, lifecycle compliance, recovery readiness, project delivery, vendor performance, and financial results to drive continual improvement.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical risk, service performance, investment needs, and project status into clear business implications, recommendations, and decision-ready reporting for executives, operational leaders, and technical teams.

  • Build a culture of reliable execution by setting realistic commitments, assigning clear owners and deadlines, tracking progress, addressing barriers early, and holding the team accountable for results. Communicate risks or delays promptly and provide recovery plans.
  • Ensure infrastructure is reliable, resilient, secure, and recoverable to support continuous business and production operations.
  • Set monitoring, alerting, capacity, and performance standards. Use service trends to identify risk, prevent recurring issues, and meet availability targets.
  • Deliver infrastructure for new plants, warehouses, offices, and expansions, aligning design, procurement, installation, testing, and readiness with construction and growth schedules.
  • Partner with Service Desk, Business Systems, Analytics, and Cybersecurity leaders to define requirements, resolve cross-functional issues, and ensure reliable business services.
  • Evaluate technology trends and recommend improvements aligned with business objectives, operational performance, and risk reduction.
  • Maintain multi-year infrastructure roadmaps; lead approved initiatives, manage risks and dependencies, and communicate progress, decisions, costs, and lifecycle needs.
  • Support budget development with forecasts, lifecycle plans, estimates, and vendor input. Manage contracts, vendors, and spending within approved budgets; report service, risk, project, vendor, and financial performance.
  • Define and execute a scalable hybrid-cloud strategy, including hosting, architecture, security, capacity, cost, and lifecycle standards. Translate business demand and resilience needs into timely infrastructure investments.
  • Enforce patching, maintenance, configuration, documentation, and lifecycle standards to keep infrastructure secure, supportable, licensed, and minimally disruptive to operations.
  • Own backup, recovery, and disaster-recovery strategies. Define recovery objectives, verify backups, test recovery, remediate gaps, and report readiness and risk.
  • Partner with Cybersecurity to implement infrastructure controls, remediate vulnerabilities, and strengthen privileged access, configuration, logging, segmentation, and incident response. Document and communicate risks and exceptions.
  • Lead infrastructure escalations, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions. Maintain support documentation and enable the Service Desk to resolve issues at the lowest appropriate level.

 

Skills and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • 10 or more years of progressively responsible infrastructure or IT operations experience, including at least 5 years leading technical teams, enterprise platforms, service providers, or major initiatives in a multi-site environment.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise networks, compute, virtualization, storage, telecommunications, databases, monitoring, backup, recovery, and related infrastructure services. Experience with VMware, SolarWinds, Microsoft SQL Server, or comparable enterprise platforms is preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, governing, and operating hybrid-cloud environments, including cloud and on-premises integration, networking, security, monitoring, cost management, capacity planning, and technology lifecycle management. Microsoft Azure experience is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting infrastructure in a multi-site manufacturing, distribution, or similarly availability-sensitive environment, including delivery of technology for new plants, warehouses, offices, or major site expansions.
  • Demonstrated ability to set direction, establish accountability, coach and develop employees, delegate effectively, manage performance, and build a collaborative, high-performing technical team.
  • Experience managing vendors, contracts, licensing, professional services, and managed-service providers, including service reviews, performance escalation, cost control, renewal planning, and operating and capital budget input.
  • Demonstrated ability to balance operational support, cybersecurity remediation, lifecycle maintenance, project delivery, construction-driven deadlines, and unplanned incidents while making clear resource and priority decisions.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain portfolio visibility, enforce change discipline, and ensure priority or commitment changes are communicated, aligned, and approved before resources are redirected.
  • Working knowledge of infrastructure security practices, including vulnerability remediation, privileged access, secure configuration, logging, network segmentation, patch governance, and incident response.
  • Experience establishing and using service and operational measures such as availability, incident trends, capacity, lifecycle compliance, recovery readiness, project delivery, vendor performance, and financial results to drive continual improvement.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical risk, service performance, investment needs, and project status into clear business implications, recommendations, and decision-ready reporting for executives, operational leaders, and technical teams.

About the Role: 
 As Kalmbach Feeds continues to grow, we are expanding our Utility team to support our busy warehouse operations. We are looking for dependable, hardworking individuals who take pride in maintaining a clean, organized, and safe facility. In this role, you will assist with general material handling, support multiple departments, and help ensure our warehouse remains efficient and well-maintained. If you enjoy staying active, working with a team, and contributing to the overall flow of daily operations, this is a great opportunity to make an impact. 

 Primary Responsibilities:
 Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

 Assist with general warehouse operations, including loading, unloading, material movement, staging, sorting, and palletizing 
 Maintain a clean and organized facility by sweeping, mopping, clearing damaged bags, breaking down cardboard, managing trash/recycling, and operating the sweeper/scrubber 
 Support production and packaging teams with material handling and restock supplies as needed 
 Operate basic warehouse equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks, hand trucks, carts) once trained 
 Follow all safety procedures and report any damaged materials, equipment issues, or safety concerns 
 Provide flexible support to multiple departments based on daily operational needs 

 Who you are: 
 Self-motivated with a strong work ethic 
 Works well independently and as part of a team 
 Dependable with an excellent attendance history 
 Takes prides in maintaining a clean and safe work environment 

 About the Company: 
 Kalmbach Feeds offers the highest quality nutritional products for livestock, poultry, and companion animals. The company was founded in 1963 by Milton and Ruth Kalmbach with a vision to develop the finest products, providing customers with the best possible nutritional value. The Kalmbach family’s traditional core values have served as the compass for consistent success for six decades, and the company has become the regional leader within the animal nutrition industry. Kalmbach Feeds enjoys an excellent reputation for quality and integrity within the animal nutrition industry and is comprised of smart self-starters who are driven to serve customers. Our experienced, talented team utilizes cutting-edge technology and proprietary processes to deliver safe, innovative products. Our stringent ingredient testing, computer automated systems, patented technologies, dedicated manufacturing facilities, and in-house nutrition specialists guarantee it. Additional information regarding our exciting company can be found at https://youtu.be/UONTNdszwY4 and www.kalmbachfeeds.com/ . 

 Kalmbach Feeds Offers: 
 Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits with eligibility on date of hire 
 401(K) (traditional and Roth options) with generous company match 
 3 Weeks Paid Time Off in first year 
 Company Paid Short Term and Long-Term Disability 
 Company Paid Life Insurance 
 Competitive Compensation 
 On Staff Life Coach 
 Medical and Dependent Care Reimbursement Plans 
 Access to Beach Front Company Condo in Fort Myers, FL 

 Kalmbach Feeds is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Each applicant for employment is considered solely based on job qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other classification protected by law. The information contained within your resume and application, including employment history, educational history, and references, are subject to verification. Pre-employment drug screen (hair and urine), physical, and criminal background check required. 

 Only qualified candidates will be contacted.

Join us in shaping the future of retail and hospitality through intelligent, scalable solutions. 

 Location: 5 days in-office, Tampa, FL 
 In this role, you will: 

 Own: Take ownership of financial processes, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and timely reporting. 

 Define: Clearly define and implement accounting policies and procedures to align with industry standards and regulatory requirements. 

 Develop: Contribute to the development and maintenance of financial systems and processes. 

 Deliver: Oversee the preparation of financial statements, budgets, and forecasts. 

 Communicate: Effectively communicate financial information to internal stakeholders and contribute to decision-making processes. 

 We are looking for someone who has: 

 Proven experience as a Staff Accountant or in a similar role. 

 Thorough knowledge of accounting principles, practices, and standards. 

 Experience with financial reporting and regulatory compliance. 

 You may be a good fit if you have these additional skills and/or educational background: 

 Bachelor's degree in Accounting , Finance, or a related field. 

 CPA certification is a plus. 

 O ur core v alues: 

 Customer – WE believe that our customers deserve the best from us every day. 

 Accountability – WE take ownership and make things happen. 

 Teamwork – WE win as a team and have fun doing it. 

 Innovation – WE innovate, inspire , ignite the future! 

 Integrity – WE are honest, ethical, and trustworthy. 

 Why Mad Mobile? 

 Mad Mobile is the #38 fastest-growing company in Florida and #9 on the Tampa Bay Times Top 100 Workplace List. We’re proud of our culture and promote diversity and a healthy work-life balance. 

 What about the benefits you ask ? 

 At Mad Mobile, we're committed to taking care of our employees right from the start. That's why there's no waiting period for our plans – they kick in from day one. We're proud to offer market leading benefits for medical, dental, and vision and cover a generous amount of your premiums. To make sure you're off to a great start, we even provide you with a $1000 HSA contribution (prorated based on your start date and split into two payments). 

 Additionally, we provide a 401(k) plan with a matching contribution of up to 4%, and the best part is you're fully vested from day one. At Mad Mobile, we're not only building the next generation of in-store experiences; we're also building the next generation of incredible teams. 

 EEOC Statement

Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, citizenship status, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition, or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws.

 This is a critical enablement function that bridges revenue teams with finance and executive leadership to ensure predictable, efficient revenue generation. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 1. Revenue Operations & Process 
 Design and implement scalable revenue operations frameworks to support Sales, Customer Success, Marketing and Partnerships, focusing on process efficiency and alignment with financial goals. 

 Optimize GTM processes, including lead routing, pipeline management, and forecasting, in collaboration with department leaders and our Restaurant GM. 

 Build and maintain scalable revenue models (e.g., SaaS ARR, GMV) to support predictable growth and align with CFO-led financial planning. 

 Implement and manage enablement tools, such as CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot), dashboards, and reporting frameworks, to enhance team productivity and visibility.
