 Streamline end-to-end revenue processes across Sales, Customer Success, and Partnerships to reduce friction and improve efficiency, ensuring a seamless customer journey. 

 Collaborate with Sales leadership to refine sales playbooks, forecast cadences, pipeline analytics and compensation plans to drive growth. 

 Partner with Customer Success to enhance retention strategies, identify upsell/cross-sell opportunities, and improve Net Revenue Retention (NRR). 

 Support Partnerships by developing scalable processes for channel enablement and affiliate programs, aligning with revenue goals. 

 3. Data-Driven Insights & Analytics 
 Establish single source of truth for key SaaS metrics: ARR, MRR, CAC, LTV, NRR, and churn 

 Build executive dashboards providing real-time visibility into revenue performance and pipeline health 

 Analyze conversion funnels to identify bottlenecks and drive measurable improvements in key metrics 

 Support board and investor communications with accurate forecasting and growth analytics 

 4. Technology & Systems Optimization 
 Manage and optimize RevOps tech stack (CRM, marketing automation, billing, analytics) 

 Drive process automation to eliminate revenue leakage and improve team productivity 

 Ensure seamless data integration and integrity across all revenue-generating systems 

 Evaluate and implement new tools to scale operations efficiently 

 5. Collaboration with Finance & Executive Leadership 
 Partner closely with the CFO to align revenue operations with financial strategy, budgeting, and forecasting processes. 

 Provide data-backed insights to support board and investor communications, including revenue forecasts, pipeline coverage, and growth metrics. 

 Act as a strategic liaison between Sales, Customer Success, Partnerships, and Finance to ensure cohesive execution of revenue initiatives. 

 Key Qualifications 
 7+ years of experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or business operations in high-growth SaaS or technology companies. 

 Proven track record of implementing scalable revenue processes and improving operational efficiency in a B2B SaaS environment. 

 Deep expertise in SaaS metrics (ARR, MRR, CAC, LTV, NRR, churn) and financial modeling, with strong analytical skills to drive data-informed decisions. 

 Proficiency with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot) and revenue operations tools, with experience optimizing tech stacks for GTM teams. 

 Exceptional communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority. 

 Strategic mindset with a focus on process automation, data integrity, and operational scalability. 

 Experience supporting financial reporting and working closely with Finance teams under a CFO’s leadership. 

 Why Mad Mobile? 
 Impact: Drive revenue operations for a fast-growing AI company transforming retail and hospitality 

 Location: Thrive in Tampa Bay's vibrant tech scene with year-round sunshine

 Growth: Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and clear advancement opportunities

We're proud to offer market leading benefits for medical, dental, and vision and cover a generous amount of your premiums. To make sure you're off to a great start, we even provide you with a $500 HSA contribution (prorated based on your start date and split into two payments). 
 Additionally, we provide a 401(k) plan with a matching contribution of up to 4% (2025), and the best part is you're fully vested from day one. At Mad Mobile, we're not only building the next generation of in-store experiences; we're also building the next generation of incredible teams.

description:
Security Officer (Night Shift)
 Full Time 
 St. Louis, MO, US (Webster Groves Campus) 
 Join Us to Build Healing and Hope Together! 
 As leaders in children’s mental health and wellness, St. Louis Children’s and KVC Health Systems Youth Mental Health Care have partnered to create one of the nation’s most innovative and transformative youth mental health and wellness campuses. The partnership includes a 77-bed acute care hospital and outpatient programs. Located on the KVC Missouri Children’s Mental Wellness Campus conveniently located in Webster Groves, Missouri, the peaceful environment and broad continuum of care allow children and families to access the appropriate level of treatment throughout their healing experience. The new campus is slated to open in late 2026. Learn more at stlouischildrenskvc.org . Join us and be a part of this journey of healing and hope for thousands of children and teens.
 Job Summary: 
 The Security Officer provides safety and security services to protect patients, visitors, staff, and property at St. Louis Children's Hospital and Camber Mental Health. This is a night shift position responsible for monitoring facility access, conducting safety rounds, and ensuring a secure environment during overnight hours. They will escort individuals, secure personal belongings, address unauthorized individuals, and help de-escalate situations in lobby and intake areas.
 Minimum Requirements: 
 Education: High school diploma or equivalent required.
 Licensure/Certification: Valid Driver’s License and auto insurance with good driving record.
 Experience: Two years of verifiable employment history related to this position, such as law enforcement, security guard, corrections, or specific military service.
 Skills: Requires intermediate skills in Microsoft Office suite, including Word, Excel, and Outlook email.
 Shift Requirement: Ability to work scheduled night shifts and maintain consistent alertness throughout the duration of the overnight assignment.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Demonstrate professionalism and respect toward colleagues, patients, and community members from diverse backgrounds.
 Patrol buildings and grounds during night hours to identify and address safety, fire, and security risks.
 Maintain a vigilant presence to monitor facility access and ensure all points of entry are secure.
 Respond to emergencies, coordinate with emergency personnel, and assist with evacuations and crowd control.
 Investigate suspicious activity, safety hazards, and security incidents on hospital property.
 Perform overnight safety checks and monitoring to support a safe environment for residents and staff.
 Assist with fire, tornado, and safety drills, including documentation and staff training.
 Inspect and maintain emergency and safety equipment, reporting any malfunctions.
 Perform additional safety and security duties as assigned to support facility operations.
 Physical & Work Environment: 
 The conditions described are representative of those required to perform this role, with reasonable accommodations available. This position involves regular standing, walking, and communication, with frequent use of hands and occasional bending or kneeling. The role may require lifting up to 10 pounds regularly, 25 pounds frequently, and 75 pounds occasionally.
 Because this is a safety-sensitive role, the employee must be able to maintain appropriate alertness and attention to perform duties safely during scheduled work hours and to respond appropriately to changing conditions. The role may involve working with patients who may exhibit unsafe behaviors or require assistance with activities of daily living. Successful completion of required training (including crisis prevention/intervention and safety hold training, as applicable) and demonstration of competency are conditions of employment for this role.
 Benefits & More: 
 Employee benefits and culture fall under the KVC Health Systems umbrella. KVC is a family of private, nonprofit organizations that strengthen families, prevent child abuse and neglect, and help people achieve mental health wellness.
 At KVC, we offer a positive, supportive workplace where each person can do work they love. KVC has an incredible 83 Work Wellbeing score on Indeed, placing us among the top 1% of employers nationally. KVC was also named #15 on Glassdoor’s Best-Led Companies 2025 list. In addition to being mission-driven, we offer employees an unparalleled level of flexibility, wellbeing, learning, and rewards.

description:
$2000 SIGN ON BONUS + $500 RETENTION BONUS 
 If you are looking for a rewarding job where you can make a difference then take a look at KVC Kentucky and all the things we do! Are you called to help those struggling with substance abuse? You can help us combat the opioid epidemic in Kentucky with a career at KVC.
 People matter, and that’s why we exist. By providing in-home behavioral healthcare, family preservation and reunification, foster care and youth substance abuse treatment, KVC Kentucky touches the lives of over 12,000 children and families each year. Our services are in-home, strengths-based, and driven by a focus on the safety, permanency, and wellbeing of the child and family.
 KVC is accredited by The Joint Commission, considered a gold standard in healthcare. Our 200+ passionate, dedicated staff working from 8 locations across the state help strengthen individuals and families each day. Join us in enriching and enhancing the lives of children and families.
 Requirements: 
 Education:
 Master’s Degree in Social Work (or a related field)
 Licensure/Certification: 
 Valid driver’s license and auto insurance; Professional license as determined by degree (ie CSW, LPCA)
 Experience:
 No previous clinical experience required but experience working with multi-problem families, familiarity with crisis intervention, and knowledge of developing behaviorally specific goals are helpful.
 Preferred Experience/Skills: 
 Requires Intermediate computer skills in typing/keyboarding, Microsoft Word and Excel programs as well as Outlook email

 POSITION SUMMARY

 The FFPRS Clinical Specialist will provide comprehensive bio-psychosocial assessment, treatment planning, and clinical services in accordance with FFPRS programming, agency standards and Family First approved evidence-based practices. The Clinical Specialist should be proficient in conducting interviews and diagnostic assessments, administering, and scoring psychometric assessments, and providing ongoing treatment utilizing KVC KY evidence-based practice models outlined in the FFPSA and Kentucky state plan. Clinical Specialists must participate in initial and ongoing training and consultation activities as required to implement evidence-based practices and must adhere to the requirements and fidelity monitoring activities outlined by the model. Clinical Specialists must be willing to provide assessment and treatment services in the home, school, and community as well as via telehealth in a trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and strengths-based manner. The Clinical Specialist must have a master's degree in Social Work (or other related field) with the ability to provide clinical services in Kentucky. The Clinical Specialist must be able to be independently licensed or provisionally licensed and under the supervision of a licensed provider.

 KVC employees are expected to work with children and families, community partners and each other using KVC values: The heart of our work is helping people. Our character is built on authenticity and compassion. Family connection drives our culture. Collaboration fuels our improvement. Urgency and innovation mark our approach. Diverse perspectives are key to our progress. Additionally, staff members are expected to be a role model for children and families, be solutions focused and build upon their strengths. KVC employees are also expected to maintain knowledge of, and adhere to, all company policies and procedures.
 ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Other duties may be assigned according to qualification of staff and development of programs.

 Direct Service
 Utilize statewide agency-approved evidence-based practice models under FFPRS contract to provide direct services in a trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and strengths-based manner to families referred to Family First Preservation & Reunification Services targeted at reducing risks, improving child well-being, and preserving child placement with the family, as identified in the family’s service plan.
 Complete face-to-face intake with client/family/caregiver according to program guidelines and initiate comprehensive assessment. 
 Provide screening and assessment services, including comprehensive assessment of family functioning, risks, and individual service needs, according to program guidelines; assessment shall result in determination of inclusion or exclusion for appropriate program and services.
 Identify treatment needs, formulate treatment recommendations, and develop a comprehensive assessment-driven treatment plan directed by program guidelines (e.g., medical necessity in BHS), best practice, and appropriate level of care recommendations.
 Review relevant records and collaborate with treatment providers and other collateral sources as part of overall assessment in order to identify client/family needs and include in treatment recommendations.
 Utilize evidence-based treatment modalities to provide therapeutic services in accordance to the assessment-driven, individualized treatment plan.
 Collaborate with the treatment team and family/client to develop a treatment/service plan to meet identified needs according to program guidelines.
 Maintain regular communication with treatment team regarding family’s participation, safety risks, identified needs, and progress in treatment.
 Develop and update safety plans, as needed, to address safety risks for the client and /or family according to program guidelines.
 Administer the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) to client and/or family members according to agency policy to assess risk for suicide and take appropriate steps to mitigate identified risks.
 Participate in collaborative team meetings with clients and their families as well as other treatment providers and community partners according to program guidelines in order to meet client/family treatment needs and develop treatment recommendations.
 Provide services that utilize agency models including evidence-based practices and clinical decision-making tools to provide clinical services to clients and/or families according to program guidelines.
 Collaborate with community mental health providers as needed to ensure continuity of care and provision of mental health services when either client/family needs require an increased or decreased level of care.
 Participate in case consultation and/or team meetings, as scheduled by program administrators, to review clients and staff high risk cases.
 Complete 3, 6, and 12 month aftercare contacts and document in ChartOnline within agency and contractual timeframes for assigned families in Family First Preservation and Reunification Services (FFPRS) program.
 Regularly travel to client/family homes and community locations in order to participate in home visits, community partner contacts, team meetings and provide therapy in the client/family natural setting. Occasional travel for training and other meetings.
 Maintain flexible schedule based on needs and availability of clients. Work time may include evenings and weekends.
 Participate in on-call rotation according to program guidelines.
 Provide mentoring to students and/or new hires as assigned.
 Continuing Education, Supervision, & Professional Development
 Create an Individual Learning Plan with Associate Director to identify required and needed areas of training in addition to areas of interest to enhance service delivery to families and clients receiving KVC services.
 Attend assigned trainings according to program guidelines.
 Attend training in trauma-informed care within 6 months of hire.
 Complete training in North Carolina Family Assessment Scale (NCFAS) and other assessment tools and fidelity measures necessary to complete job functions.
 Attend training in state-approved Family First evidence-based practices as required by agency and participate in all training related activities including, but not limited to, consultations and case presentations.
 Attend training in EBP fidelity measures necessary to complete EBP supervision, coaching, consultation, or to complete EBPmonitoring tools as required by the EBP or agency model implementation.
 Attend meetings, seminars, and other educational functions of the agency as identified by supervisor.
 Participate in individual and/or group supervision as required by licensing board.
 Obtain 40 CEUs per year, including 20 by June 30.
 Complete assigned UKG Pro Learning courses by given deadlines.
 Complete all CEUs required to maintain professional license, as applicable.
 Maintain professional licensing and certification as identified by the supervisor or agency director and state regulations.
 Record Keeping & Documentation
 Maintain and submit records in ChartOnline (electronic records system) for the purpose of quality assurance, documentation of service delivery, and agency billing. Documentation can include, but may not be limited to, the following: screenings; psychosocial and family assessments; treatment/service plans; progress notes; non-billable contacts; aftercare plans; and discharge/termination summaries, in accordance with all applicable regulations, contract and grant requirements.
 Document all referrals made to outside agencies and client/family compliance with these referrals.
 Utilize collaborative documentation to complete service tickets and other documentation and forms while in session with clients and/or guardians to ensure client involvement with treatment.
 Complete program-specific case documentation in accordance with agency policy and contractual timeframes. Ensure accuracy of all documentation completed.
 Complete Service Tickets and other documentation in ChartOnline in accordance with agency and program deadlines.
 Upload case-related documentation to ChartOnline in accordance with agency requirements.
 Complete all needed Managed Care Organization, Insurance or Payor documentation needed to ensure approved service delivery or appeal decisions for behavior health services. 
 Provide progress reports for each case that has DCBS involvement to DCBS personnel in accordance with program guidelines and as requested by DCBS.
 Submit receipts weekly and in accordance with submission policy.
 Enter case information into the In-Home Services Database, as needed, if required by program (FPRS).
 Complete documentation and follow through of all individual supervision, group supervision, and case consultation in keeping with regulations, contract and agency standards.
 Special Projects
 Assist with any special duties or responsibilities assigned by agency director or another member of management.
 Professional Performance & Conduct
 Meet expectations as defined in the Performance Evaluation and Competency Checklists.
 Dress professionally as outlined in the KVC Employee Manual.
 Maintain confidentiality of client and agency information. All KVC employees are privy to confidential client information. Due to complex treatment needs of our clients, service providers have contacts that require written and verbal information exchange with different professionals and agencies. A strict code of behavior must be maintained to protect the special nature of divulged information.
 Follow reporting laws. When a child is endangered, in areas of health, neglect, physical and/or sexual abuse, all staff members are legally obligated to report that information to authorities. 
 Maintain client rights as outlined in agency manuals.
 Follow risk management policies as outlined in agency manuals.
 Follow KVC emergency and safety procedures as outlined in agency manuals.
 Maintain a current driver’s license and automobile insurance (as required by agency’s insurer). 
 Maintain professional behavior and attitude when interacting with management, colleagues, clients, and community partners in any setting.
 Follow code of ethics of one’s profession (e.g., Social Work, Psychology, Counselors, Marriage & Family Therapists).

 PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

 The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
 While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, talk or hear, and taste or smell. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee is occasionally required to sit. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

 WORK ENVIRONMENT

 The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 
 While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

 Click "Apply Now" to begin the hiring process! 
 Funding for this position provided through the Cabinet for Health & Family Services with Kentucky State Funds and/or Federal Funds.
 KVC is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age or disability.

  • Complete 3, 6, and 12 month aftercare contacts and document in ChartOnline within agency and contractual timeframes for assigned families in Family First Preservation and Reunification Services (FFPRS) program.
  • Regularly travel to client/family homes and community locations in order to participate in home visits, community partner contacts, team meetings and provide therapy in the client/family natural setting. Occasional travel for training and other meetings.
  • Maintain flexible schedule based on needs and availability of clients. Work time may include evenings and weekends.
  • Participate in on-call rotation according to program guidelines.
  • Provide mentoring to students and/or new hires as assigned.

Continuing Education, Supervision, & Professional Development

Create an Individual Learning Plan with Associate Director to identify required and needed areas of training in addition to areas of interest to enhance service delivery to families and clients receiving KVC services.

Attend assigned trainings according to program guidelines.

Attend training in trauma-informed care within 6 months of hire.

Complete training in North Carolina Family Assessment Scale (NCFAS) and other assessment tools and fidelity measures necessary to complete job functions.

Attend training in state-approved Family First evidence-based practices as required by agency and participate in all training related activities including, but not limited to, consultations and case presentations.

Attend training in EBP fidelity measures necessary to complete EBP supervision, coaching, consultation, or to complete EBPmonitoring tools as required by the EBP or agency model implementation.

Attend meetings, seminars, and other educational functions of the agency as identified by supervisor.

Participate in individual and/or group supervision as required by licensing board.

Obtain 40 CEUs per year, including 20 by June 30.

Complete assigned UKG Pro Learning courses by given deadlines.

Complete all CEUs required to maintain professional license, as applicable.

Maintain professional licensing and certification as identified by the supervisor or agency director and state regulations.

Record Keeping & Documentation

Maintain and submit records in ChartOnline (electronic records system) for the purpose of quality assurance, documentation of service delivery, and agency billing. Documentation can include, but may not be limited to, the following: screenings; psychosocial and family assessments; treatment/service plans; progress notes; non-billable contacts; aftercare plans; and discharge/termination summaries, in accordance with all applicable regulations, contract and grant requirements.

Document all referrals made to outside agencies and client/family compliance with these referrals.

Utilize collaborative documentation to complete service tickets and other documentation and forms while in session with clients and/or guardians to ensure client involvement with treatment.

Complete program-specific case documentation in accordance with agency policy and contractual timeframes. Ensure accuracy of all documentation completed.

Complete Service Tickets and other documentation in ChartOnline in accordance with agency and program deadlines.

Upload case-related documentation to ChartOnline in accordance with agency requirements.

Complete all needed Managed Care Organization, Insurance or Payor documentation needed to ensure approved service delivery or appeal decisions for behavior health services.  

Provide progress reports for each case that has DCBS involvement to DCBS personnel in accordance with program guidelines and as requested by DCBS.

Submit receipts weekly and in accordance with submission policy.

Enter case information into the In-Home Services Database, as needed, if required by program (FPRS).

Complete documentation and follow through of all individual supervision, group supervision, and case consultation in keeping with regulations, contract and agency standards.

Special Projects

Assist with any special duties or responsibilities assigned by agency director or another member of management.

Professional Performance & Conduct

Meet expectations as defined in the Performance Evaluation and Competency Checklists.

Dress professionally as outlined in the KVC Employee Manual.

Maintain confidentiality of client and agency information. All KVC employees are privy to confidential client information. Due to complex treatment needs of our clients, service providers have contacts that require written and verbal information exchange with different professionals and agencies. A strict code of behavior must be maintained to protect the special nature of divulged information.

Follow reporting laws. When a child is endangered, in areas of health, neglect, physical and/or sexual abuse, all staff members are legally obligated to report that information to authorities. 

Maintain client rights as outlined in agency manuals.

Follow risk management policies as outlined in agency manuals.

Follow KVC emergency and safety procedures as outlined in agency manuals.

Maintain a current driver’s license and automobile insurance (as required by agency’s insurer). 

Maintain professional behavior and attitude when interacting with management, colleagues, clients, and community partners in any setting.

Follow code of ethics of one’s profession (e.g., Social Work, Psychology, Counselors, Marriage & Family Therapists).

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, talk or hear, and taste or smell.  The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  The employee is occasionally required to sit.  The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds.  Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.  

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to outside weather conditions.  The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

KVC is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age or disability.

Art Therapist (Full-Time) 
 Full Time
 St. Louis, MO, US

 *This position is offering a $5,000 sign on bonus, paid in three increments across six months of successful employment!

 Join Us to Build Healing and Hope Together! 
 As leaders in children’s mental health and wellness, St. Louis Children’s and KVC Health Systems Youth Mental Health Care have partnered to create one of the nation’s most innovative and transformative youth mental health and wellness campuses. The partnership includes a 77-bed acute care hospital and outpatient programs. Located on the KVC Missouri Children’s Mental Wellness Campus conveniently located in Webster Groves, Missouri, the peaceful environment and broad continuum of care allow children and families to access the appropriate level of treatment throughout their healing experience. The new campus is slated to open in late 2026. Learn more at stlouischildrenskvc.org. Join us and be a part of this journey of healing and hope for thousands of children and teens. 

 Job Summary 
 The Art Therapist will implement trauma-informed and therapeutic activities within the creative process of art making to enhance the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of the children and youth receiving residential services. Therapist will collaborate as an active member of the treatment team. 
 Minimum Requirements: 
 Education: 
 A Master’s Degree from an accredited college or university in Art Therapy, Counseling, Marriage and Family Therapy, Social Work, or Psychology, with supervised post-graduate art therapy experience.
 Licensure/Certification: 
 Art Therapist - Registered (ATR) or Board Certified Art Therapist (ATR-BC) required 
 Valid driver’s license and auto insurance 
 Experience:
 Supervised post-graduate art therapy experience. Requires intermediate computer skills in typing/keyboarding, Microsoft Word and Excel programs as well as Outlook email. 
 Preferred Experience/Skills: 
 Six months to one year experience. Preference given to experience providing art therapy to youth receiving mental health services.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Additional duties may be assigned based on organizational needs and staff qualifications. 

 Physical & Work Environment
 This role involves a mix of standing, walking, and occasional lifting, along with regular use of office equipment. You’ll work in a professional office setting with moderate noise levels and occasional exposure to outdoor conditions.
 If you’re ready to take ownership of a critical role that keeps operations running smoothly while making a meaningful impact on people’s lives, we encourage you to apply.

 Benefits & More 
 Employee benefits and culture fall under the KVC Health Systems umbrella. KVC is a family of private, nonprofit organizations that strengthen families, prevent child abuse and neglect, and help people achieve mental health wellness. Through our broad continuum of care, we are proud to be a national leader in mental health, child welfare, and health and human services transformation. 

 At KVC, we offer a positive, supportive workplace where each person can do work they love. In fact, we’re so proud of our culture that we see it as our top competitive advantage in the health and human services field. Based on the voice of our employees, KVC has an incredible 83 Work Wellbeing score on Indeed, a rating so high and rare that it places KVC among the top 1% of employers nationally. KVC was also named #15 on Glassdoor’s Best-Led Companies 2025 list, a recognition achieved entirely based on anonymous employee reviews. In addition to being mission-driven, we offer employees an unparalleled level of flexibility, wellbeing, learning, inclusion, recognition, and rewards

Under general supervision, this position creates truss / wall placement plans, design drawings and quotes along with providing technical support for Division Superintendent’s related to truss /wall components for residential projects.

Reporting Relationships:
• Reports to Engineer Manager

Duties and Responsibilities:
• Produces wall, floor and roof truss placement plans, truss design drawings and truss quotes using your ability to understand blueprints plans of house projects.
• Determine design specifications based on blueprints and structural design needs.
• Review other designers work as part of a double check system to reduce design errors prior to putting paperwork into manufacturing.
• Create shop paperwork that is optimized and batched for efficiency based on equipment used in manufacturing.
• Communicate with staff on technical aspects of the designs which require clarifi-cation from Architect or Engineer. Document communication with said parties us-ing excel spreadsheet and saved emails.
• Consult with more experienced component technicians and management when more in-depth analysis is required.
• Plan and pace your own work efficiency in order to meet daily, weekly, project, or team related productivity goals.
• Understand and observe all safety procedures and practices in order to prevent injury to self or co-workers; attend periodic safety meetings as required; recom-mend changes to improve safety procedures.
• Other duties may be assigned.

Required Education:
• High school diploma or General Education Degree (GED)

Desired Experience:
• One (1) year component design experience; or equivalent experience and educa-tion.
• Mitek Software required with Sapphire experience for at least one year

Skills and Abilities:
• Knowledge of company products sufficient to determine appropriate structural ap-plications
• Strong attention to detail
• Knowledge of basic math and measurement skills
• Knowledge of drafting, architectural design or CAD applications
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite

Work Conditions/Physical Requirements
• Office Environment
• Must be able to remain in a stationary position 75% of time

 Steel City Title, part of Maronda Homes, is a multi-state Title and Settlement company helping homeowners, mortgage lenders and real estate agents with the settlement process. Our core principle is keeping clients happy through our consistently smooth and efficient closing process. We are looking for Licensed Title Agent/Closer to join our exciting and growing team of Title Professionals for a remote opportunity supporting our Pennsylvania Branch.
 Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
  Reviewing contracts.
  Responsible for researching property records and preparing documents and information for real estate transactions.
  Opening and ordering searches for files.
  Importing title searches.
  Preparing title commitments, closing disclosures.
  Preparing buyer and seller documents.
  Clearing title issues (i.e. lien, quite title, title vesting issues, etc.).
  Communicate with buyers to confirm correct information for contacts.
  Communicate with realtor to confirm correct transactional information.
  Other duties as required.

  Two years of experience with real estate transactions, title processing or as a title company processor is essential.

  Reliable and detail oriented.

  Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  Familiarity with preparing Closing Disclosures.
  Provide a high level of customer service, including the building of strong relationships with our customers and colleagues.
  Currently a Licensed Title Agent in Pennsylvania is preferred.

job_title: CDL A - Drop and Hook Driver
description:
About Us: 

 Liberty Tire Recycling is a high-growth company and the premier provider of tire recycling services in North America with operations throughout the United States and Canada. Liberty Tire annually transforms more than 210 million tires into raw materials for smart, sustainable products that improve our environment and people’s lives. The Company is private equity owned, has approximately 60 sites in the US and Canada, and nearly 4,000 employees. With innovative tools, technologies and processes, Liberty Tire is a revolutionary American conservation enterprise – from coast to coast, and from whole tire to end products. The company’s commitment to finding new and better ways to RECLAIM, RECYCLE and REUSE bridges the sustainability goals of scrap tire generators nationwide with those of local scrap rubber consumers. 

 Job Summary: 
The Class A CDL Driver - Drop & Hook is responsible for the safe and timely pickup, transport, and delivery of trailers using drop and hook operations. Routes are assigned by dispatch; drivers are responsible for managing daily transportation activities, maintaining professionalism at customer locations, and completing all required documentation accurately. This role requires strict compliance with DOT, FMCSA, and Liberty Tire Recycling safety and operational requirements. 
 Duties and Responsibilites: 
 Safely transport trailers between customer locations and designated Liberty Tire Recycling facilities or approved disposal sites.
 Perform drop and hook trailer operations, including exchanging loaded and empty trailers at customer locations, company yards, and facilities.
 Ensure all loads are properly secured and compliant with DOT and company safety requirements prior to transport.
 Conduct required pre‑trip, post‑trip, and en‑route inspections of assigned tractors and trailers; complete DVIRs and report maintenance or safety concerns immediately.
 Accurately complete DOT logs, driver qualification documentation, bills of lading, manifests, and required company or customer paperwork.
 Collect and transport payments from cash‑only customers when required, in accordance with company cash‑handling procedures.
 Maintain clean, safe, and operational equipment at all times.
 Navigate assigned routes using maps, GPS, and dispatch instructions while accounting for traffic, weather, and site conditions.
 Maintain professional and courteous interactions with customers, dispatch, and internal teams.
 Follow all Liberty Tire Recycling safety policies, environmental standards, and operational procedures.
 Assist with yard moves, trailer positioning, and other transportation‑related tasks as assigned.
 Perform additional duties as required to support operations.
 Skills and Abilities: 
 Working knowledge of DOT and FMCSA regulations.
 Ability to safely operate Class A equipment and perform drop and hook operations.
 Strong attention to safety, accuracy, and compliance.
 Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
 Clear and professional communication with dispatch, customers, and coworkers.
 Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and perform physical tasks related to inspections and equipment handling.
 Required Qualifications: 
 Minimum age of 22 years old.
 Valid Class A Commercial Driver’s License (CDL).
 Must meet all FMCSA driver qualification requirements.
 Acceptable Motor Vehicle Record in compliance with DOT standards.
 Minimum of 1 year of commercial driving experience or equivalent Class A CDL driving experience.
 Work Environments and Physical Demands: 
This role requires extended periods of driving, work outdoors in varying weather conditions, and physical tasks associated with inspections and trailer handling operations. 
 Benefits: 
 401(k) 
 Dental insurance 
 Health insurance 
 Paid time off 
 Vision insurance 
 EEO Statement: 
 Liberty Tire Recycling is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, relationship or association with a protected veteran (spouses or other family members), genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

 This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced talent management professional with expertise in learning and development, recruiting and onboarding, and programs that create po siti ve ca ndidate and employee experience s .  RESPONSIBILITIES

description:
THE OPPORTUNITY 

 The National League of Cities is an organization based in Washington, D.C., comprised of city, town, and village leaders across the country focused on improving the quality of life for their current and future constituents. With over 100 years of dedication to local governments' strength, health, and advancement, NLC has gained the trust and support of more than 2,000 cities, towns, and villages nationwide. We are a dynamic and forward-thinking organization dedicated to supporting municipal leaders and driving positive change in communities across the nation. 

 POSITION OVERVIEW 

 The National League of Cities (NLC) is seeking a Program Manager, Strategic Partnerships to support the growth, engagement, and success of NLC's strategic partnership portfolio. This position will manage an assigned portfolio of strategic partners while leading business development efforts to identify, cultivate, and secure new partnerships and sponsorship opportunities. This is a revenue-generating role with direct responsibility for contributing to the growth of NLC’s partnership and sponsorship revenue.
 The Program Manager will build strong relationships with current and prospective partners, identify opportunities that align private-sector organizations with the needs and priorities of cities, towns, and villages, and contribute to the continued growth of NLC's Strategic Partnerships program.
 This role is ideal for a relationship-driven professional who enjoys building connections, developing new opportunities, and translating organizational priorities into mutually beneficial partnerships.

 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

 Partnership Management & Engagement 
 Serve as the primary relationship manager for an assigned portfolio of Executive, Capstone, Sponsorship, and other strategic partners.
 Develop and execute partner engagement, stewardship, and renewal strategies that strengthen relationships and deliver value to NLC partners.
 Work collaboratively with partners to understand their goals and identify opportunities for meaningful engagement across NLC programs, events, and initiatives.
 Coordinate with internal NLC teams to ensure successful delivery of partnership benefits and commitments.
 Monitor partner engagement and identify opportunities to strengthen, expand, and renew existing relationships.
 Business Development & Partner Outreach 
 Research, identify, and qualify prospective sponsors and strategic partners whose priorities align with NLC's mission, programs, and membership.
 Build and manage a robust pipeline of prospective partnership opportunities through proactive outreach, networking, referrals, industry engagement, and other business development activities.
 Cultivate relationships with prospective partners and serve as an initial point of contact for new partnership opportunities.
 Conduct discovery meetings to understand prospective partners' goals and identify opportunities for engagement with NLC.
 Develop partnership proposals, presentations, and other business development materials in collaboration with the Strategic Partnerships Director.
 Support partnership negotiations, contracting, and onboarding of newly secured partners.
 Collaborate with NLC's Marketing, Events, Programs, and other teams to identify and develop sponsorship opportunities across conferences, programs, events, and initiatives.
 Pipeline & Performance Management 
 Maintain accurate and timely records of prospects, outreach activities, partnership opportunities, and next steps within NLC's CRM.
 Track business development activity, pipeline metrics, revenue opportunities, and forecasts.
 Provide regular updates on prospect activity, partnership opportunities, and progress toward departmental revenue goals.
 Support the transition of newly secured partners into ongoing relationship management while maintaining continuity and long-term engagement.
 What We're Looking For 
 The successful candidate will be a proactive relationship builder who is comfortable developing new connections, managing multiple priorities, and working collaboratively across an organization. They will bring curiosity, initiative, strong communication skills, and an ability to understand the priorities of both private-sector organizations and local government leaders. Candidates should be comfortable operating in a sales function, as they will be directly responsible for generating revenue to support the critical work of the National League of Cities.
 The ideal candidate will be energized by identifying new opportunities and building relationships from the ground up while also providing a high level of service and engagement to existing partners.
 Role Impact 
 This position plays an important role in expanding NLC's Strategic Partnerships portfolio and strengthening the value delivered to existing partners. By combining relationship management with proactive business development, the Program Manager will help generate sustainable revenue, cultivate new organizational relationships, and create partnerships that connect private-sector expertise and resources with the priorities of America's cities, towns, and villages.
 NLC INCLUSION STATEMENT 
 NLC is committed to fostering a culture that values diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences.
 NLC is dedicated to ensuring that our hiring practices and workplace policies provide equal access to opportunities, skill development, and merit-based advancement. 
 By embracing inclusion, we foster a work culture of continuous learning, innovation, creativity, and understanding which are essential to our success supporting cities, towns, and villages.

 WORK LOCATION 
 This hybrid position is based in Washington, DC, and requires three days on-site at our NLC headquarters. 
 SALARY RANGE 
 $65,000-$75,000 annually

 OUR BENEFITS 
 Competitive benefits and retirement package 
 Generous paid time off and holidays 
 Hybrid work environment 
 Professional Development 

 EOE/M/F/D/V

GL Accountant 
 Centreville, VA (Full-Time, On-site) 
 Position Summary
 We are seeking a detail-oriented and self-directed GL Accountant to support core accounting and treasury functions, who will be primary responsible for completing bank reconciliations, cash management activities, general ledger accounting, and various balance sheet account reconciliations.
 This role requires strong analytical abilities, sound understanding of U.S. GAAP, and the ability to independently investigate and resolve discrepancies by identifying underlying transactions and supporting documentation. The ideal candidate will be comfortable drafting reconciliations from start to finish, maintaining supporting schedules, and actively contributing to a timely and accurate month-end close process.
 This position provides opportunities to contribute meaningfully to system of internal controls and engage in process optimization, while partnering with team members across Finance, Payroll, Operations, and other business functions.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Perform full-cycle daily and monthly bank reconciliations for multiple accounts.
 Research and resolve reconciling items by identifying source documentation, tracing transactions through operational systems, and applying correct accounting treatment.
 Maintain organized documentation for deposits in transit, outstanding checks, bank fees, ACH activity, and other reconciling items.
 Assist preparation and maintenance of daily cash reporting and cash-flow forecasting.
 Monitor cash activity and support treasury management initiatives.
 Utilize banking platforms to research cash transactions and support reconciliation and reporting activities.
 Prepare and maintain reconciliations for varied balance sheet accounts including cash, prepaids, accruals, fixed assets, and other assigned accounts.
 Investigate variances and aging reconciling items and propose corrective actions.
 Support month-end and year-end close activities through preparation of journal entries, reconciliations, supporting schedules, and close checklists.
 Ensure assigned close deliverables are completed accurately and on schedule.
 Support the design, documentation, and implementation of internal controls related to cash management and reconciliation processes.
 Identify opportunities to improve reconciliation processes, reporting efficiency, documentation standards, and internal control effectiveness.
 Support internal, external audits through preparation of reconciliation support, schedules, and analysis.
 Utilize accounting systems effectively and recommend process improvements to enhance efficiency and accuracy.

 Qualifications
 Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance required.
 3+ years of practical experience with direct responsibility for bank reconciliations, general ledger accounting, and month-end close activities.
 Proven record of preparing accurate account reconciliations while managing competing priorities and meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
 Ability to independently resolve complex reconciling differences.
 Strong understanding of U.S. GAAP and financial reporting principles.
 Experience preparing balance sheet account reconciliations, including cash, prepaids, accruals, and other general ledger accounts.

GL Accountant

Centreville, VA (Full-Time, On-site)

Position Summary

We are seeking a detail-oriented and self-directed GL Accountant to support core accounting and treasury functions, who will be primary responsible for completing bank reconciliations, cash management activities, general ledger accounting, and various balance sheet account reconciliations.

This role requires strong analytical abilities, sound understanding of U.S. GAAP, and the ability to independently investigate and resolve discrepancies by identifying underlying transactions and supporting documentation. The ideal candidate will be comfortable drafting reconciliations from start to finish, maintaining supporting schedules, and actively contributing to a timely and accurate month-end close process.

This position provides opportunities to contribute meaningfully to system of internal controls and engage in process optimization, while partnering with team members across Finance, Payroll, Operations, and other business functions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform full-cycle daily and monthly bank reconciliations for multiple accounts.
  • Research and resolve reconciling items by identifying source documentation, tracing transactions through operational systems, and applying correct accounting treatment.
  • Maintain organized documentation for deposits in transit, outstanding checks, bank fees, ACH activity, and other reconciling items.
  • Assist preparation and maintenance of daily cash reporting and cash-flow forecasting.
  • Monitor cash activity and support treasury management initiatives.
  • Utilize banking platforms to research cash transactions and support reconciliation and reporting activities.
  • Prepare and maintain reconciliations for varied balance sheet accounts including cash, prepaids, accruals, fixed assets, and other assigned accounts.
  • Investigate variances and aging reconciling items and propose corrective actions.
  • Support month-end and year-end close activities through preparation of journal entries, reconciliations, supporting schedules, and close checklists.
  • Ensure assigned close deliverables are completed accurately and on schedule.
  • Support the design, documentation, and implementation of internal controls related to cash management and reconciliation processes.
  • Identify opportunities to improve reconciliation processes, reporting efficiency, documentation standards, and internal control effectiveness.
  • Support internal, external audits through preparation of reconciliation support, schedules, and analysis.
  • Utilize accounting systems effectively and recommend process improvements to enhance efficiency and accuracy.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance required.
  • 3+ years of practical experience with direct responsibility for bank reconciliations, general ledger accounting, and month-end close activities.
  • Proven record of preparing accurate account reconciliations while managing competing priorities and meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to independently resolve complex reconciling differences.
  • Strong understanding of U.S. GAAP and financial reporting principles.
  • Experience preparing balance sheet account reconciliations, including cash, prepaids, accruals, and other general ledger accounts.

  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and maintain detailed supporting documentation.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and take ownership of assigned responsibilities with minimal supervision.

Looking for a job in the heart of South Reno? 
 Pacific Cheese has been family owned and operated for over 50 years. We offer a generous and affordable benefits package including health, dental and vision. We also provide AD&D, LTD, STD, Employee Life Insurance at no cost. In addition to paid vacation, sick and holiday time as well as a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match. 
 We're currently hiring Production Leads for 2nd shift starting 2:00pm Monday-Friday (occasional overtime) 
 Starting Pay $27.00/HR. This starting pay includes an additional $1.50/hr for working 2nd shift. 
 SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITY: 
 Will act as a lead person who provides advice or assistance to supervisor. Capable of safe operations and training of other employees on every procedure and piece of equipment in area of responsibility. Responsible for the safe and efficient operation of their assigned area, assist in other areas as appropriate. Will conduct spot checks of finished goods to verify compliance with specifications. Will fill in as needed in line positions to support production demands. Assists Production Supervisor with accident investigations and corrective action reports. Establish and maintain effective working relationships with team members, provide guidance to trainees. Use good judgment and common sense while performing duties. 

 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 • Confirm that necessary production material is available to complete production schedule. 
 • Confirm that all equipment is prepared for production schedule. 
 • View raw material to ensure that it meets necessary quality standards. Work with Quality Assurance to make sure that input and output meets written specifications. 
 • Assist line workers to complete planned production schedule. 
 • Troubleshoot if problems occur on the line. Confer with production supervisors with any issues. 
 • At completion of production schedule ensure that production material has been returned to its correct location. 
 • Gather production records from in-feed and pack-off, verify production count, and make notes of any problems and downtime, if Supervisor is not available/out. 
 • Create production reports, perform data entry and record keeping as needed. 
 • Take initiative for identifying areas of improvement within the department, troubleshooting and working with management in resolving problems that arise. 
 • Provide advice and assistance, including on the job training and coaching to improve the overall efficiency and effectiveness of the function and the department. 
 • Ensure that safe work practices are observed with machinery. Follow Good Manufacturing Practices to ensure food safety, safe work practices to protect yourself and others and not engage in unsafe behavior. 
 • Must attend all department and company required trainings 
 • Perform other duties as assigned. 
 REQUIREMENTS/WORK CONDITIONS: Work is performed in a warehouse/production type atmosphere where the temperature is as low as 32 degrees (typically 45-55 degrees). Noise level in production environment may require the use of hearing protection. Requires standing for long period of time frequently twisting, turning, bending, stooping, pushing, pulling and lifting material up to 50lbs. 
 Pacific Cheese is a drug free workplace; pre-employment includes drug screen. 
 Pacific Cheese is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status or any other characteristic prohibited by federal, state or local laws

About Us: New York Edge is the largest provider of after-school and summer camp programs in New York City public schools. Each year, academic programs—including STEM, the arts, sports and wellness, and college access—help 40,000 students develop leadership skills and succeed in school. Working parents count on our programs to provide safe and enriching environments for their children. 

 Summary: 
 New York Edge is seeking passionate and enthusiastic people to fill the part-time role of after-school Academic Enrichment Coach. In this role, you will be critical to the successful operation of New York Edge's after-school program. You will be responsible for providing a safe and positive environment for school-age children and providing opportunities for learning, interaction, and academic/personal growth. Academic Enrichment Coaches also participate in activities and trips while providing and maintaining a safe working environment. They help with homework and prepare students to demonstrate newly acquired skills in Sports and Arts. 

 Schedule: 
 Part-Time 
 Monday – Friday 
 2:30 pm – 5:30 pm 

 This role requires you to be in person. 

 Pay: 
 $18.00/hr 

 Job Type: 
 Part-Time 

 Essential Job Functions: 
 Provide appropriate supervision at all times to ensure the health, safety, and well-being of program participants. 

 Be an agent of safety for campers. This includes taking responsibility for one’s well-being and the well-being of others. 

 Keep the immediate supervisor informed daily of any concerns regarding participants, staff, or the facility. 

 Engage participants in meaningful activities, lesson plans, and special events that are structured, age-appropriate, fun, exciting, and challenging and based on values in the areas of arts, STEM, character development, literacy, creative expression, community service, physical fitness, and/or nutrition. 

 Prepare the learning environment and necessary supplies for program activities. Assume responsibility for the cleanliness and organization of the camp room, program supplies, and activity space. 

 Support the planning and implementation of all activities, including but not limited to learning initiatives, field trips, and culminating performances. 

 Provide support to Activity Specialists with activity implementation. 

 Create and maintain a strength-based, youth-focused atmosphere that is consistent and sensitive to the needs of participants with learning, emotional, or behavioral differences. 

 Serve as a positive role model for participants. 

 Develop and maintain positive relationships with parents and guardians through regular communication about their child’s strengths and areas of growth. Take a leadership role in providing regular updates to caregivers. 

 Attend all required training sessions. Actively participate in training sessions, designated meetings, and special events. 

 Ensure that groups are in ratio. 

 Required Skills: 
 Possess a desire to work directly with children 

 Ability to work as a team member 

 Responsible, friendly, enthusiastic, actively engaged, and patient 

 Ability to follow directions and adhere to all policies/procedures 

 Open to feedback with a desire to grow professionally 

 Must have reliable communication/computer devices at home with the capacity to access the internet consistently to respond to organizational emails as well as complete training before the start of work (if needed) 

 Qualifications: 
 Must be at least 18 years old 

 High School Diploma required; some college preferred 

 Experience working with children strongly preferred 

 Work Environment & Physical Demands: 
 May be required to walk up and down stairs. 
 May have to lift or move objects/materials as needed. 
 Work is performed mostly within a New York City Public School but may be required to interact with community at-large during trips or events. 

 The Academic Enrichment Coach will be required to report to the school and interact with staff, students, parents, and the school administration. 

 At the time of offer and acceptance, the job requires safety and security clearances through the Department of Education and Department of Health. 

 New York Edge is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. 

 Disclaimer: The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the employee in this position. These statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of a person in this position.

 Role Responsibilities and Management Plan 
 Purpose of the Role

 The role operates on a train-the-trainer model. Senior Content Specialists are not primarily site-facing coaches; they build the capacity of the Content Specialists who coach in the field. Both roles support instruction across all content areas rather than specializing in one. They translate CIT curriculum, standards, and instructional targets into the professional development, coaching practices, and quality expectations their team carries to sites. 
 Core Responsibility Areas 
 The role has five core areas of responsibility. Together they define what a Senior Content Specialist owns. 
 1. Team Leadership and Supervision 
 Direct supervision and professional growth of a team of 5 to 8 Content Specialists. 
 Set clear, measurable expectations for Content Specialist performance and hold the team accountable to them 

 Conduct weekly check-ins and maintain a consistent accountability structure for a field-based team 

 Apply appropriate supervision models (directive, collaborative, consultative) to each team member's needs 

 Identify early signs of performance concern and respond promptly and supportively 

 Build a positive, collaborative team culture across a dispersed group 

 2. Professional Development Design and Implementation 
 Ownership of the PD implementation plan for the Content Specialists in the portfolio. 
 Design and deliver professional development grounded in adult learning principles 

 Manage the PD implementation plan, so every Content Specialist progresses through required training 

 Translate CIT curriculum and instructional targets into practical, teachable coaching moves 

 Use observation and coaching data to decide what PD the team needs next 

 Track completion and growth, and adjust the plan as gaps emerge 

 3. Coaching the Coaches 
 Building the coaching capability of each Content Specialist through modeling and feedback. 
 Conduct joint learning walks and co-observations to calibrate the team's observation quality 

 Review Content Specialists' observation reports and coaching logs, and give written coaching feedback 

 Model strong coaching conversations and instructional feedback 

 Support Content Specialists in reading lesson plans, pacing, and differentiating for diverse learners 

 Ensure consistency in how the team documents and reports coaching and observation notes 

 4. Instructional Quality Across Content Areas 
 Uphold instructional quality across all content areas the team supports. 
 Maintain working knowledge of the NYE curriculum and expected student outcomes across all content areas 

 Set and uphold instructional quality standards across all assigned sites in the portfolio 

 Review seasonal quality data and identify portfolio-wide patterns to inform training decisions 

 Flag curriculum gaps and recommend improvements to the relevant CIT Directors 

 Champion faithful integration of approved activity offerings across the team's sites 

 5. Hiring and Talent Support 
 Helping the department manage the volume of instructor recruitment. 
 Assist with interviewing and selecting new instructors across content areas 

 Support onboarding of new Content Specialists into the team and the CIT model 

 Contribute to the pipeline of instructional talent within the portfolio 

 The Management Plan 
 This section describes how a Senior Content Specialist manages and develops their team throughout the year: the rhythm of supervision, the flow of information, and how performance is developed. 
 Rhythm of Supervision 
 The management relationship runs on a predictable cadence so nothing depends on chance encounters. The Senior Content Specialist holds a standing weekly touchpoint with each Content Specialist, layered with monthly and seasonal checkpoints. 
 Rhythm 
 With the Content Specialist team 
 Up to Program Director & CIT Director 

 Weekly 
 30-minute check-in with each Content Specialist; review coaching logs and observation reports; remove barriers 
 Report team progress, site-level patterns, and emerging concerns to the Program Director and CIT Director 

 Monthly 
 Deliver PD sessions for the team; conduct joint learning walks at priority sites 
 Submit a monthly quality summary; flag training needs surfacing across the portfolio 

 Seasonally 
 Review each Content Specialist's caseload outcomes; set next-season coaching goals 
 Contribute to network-wide training decisions and calibration across the portfolios 

 Annually 
 Complete performance reviews; build individual development plans for the team 
 Recommend structural and curricular improvements based on the year's data 

 How Performance Is Grown 
 Supervision is developmental first. The Senior Content Specialist differentiates support based on what the coaching logs and observation reports reveal, giving newer Content Specialists closer modeling and stronger practitioners more autonomy and stretch. Performance concerns are named early, documented clearly, and addressed with a concrete improvement plan rather than left to accumulate. 
 Information Flow 
 The Senior Content Specialist is the hub between the field and leadership. Coaching notes and observation data logged by Content Specialists in the NYE Edge platform roll up into the Senior Content Specialist's monthly quality summary, which informs both the team's next PD and the network-wide decisions made with the Program Director and CIT Director. In the other direction, curriculum updates, standards, and training priorities flow from CIT leadership through the Senior Content Specialist to the team. 
 Decision Rights 
 Within their portfolio, the Senior Content Specialist decides the team's PD sequence, coaching priorities, and quality expectations, and manages day-to-day performance. Decisions that change the curriculum, staffing structure, or network-wide policy are made in consultation with CIT leadership. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 A Senior Content Specialist is succeeding when: 
 Every Content Specialist on the team is progressing through their PD plan and improving in observed coaching quality 

 Observation and coaching documentation across the team is consistent, specific, and timely 

 Activity Specialists across the team's sites show measurable instructional growth 

 Quality data flows reliably up to CIT leadership and shapes real training decisions 

 The team operates as a coherent, supported group rather than a set of isolated field staff

Job Summary: 
 This position is responsible for designing, delivering, and owning complex, production-grade enterprise applications and artificial intelligence systems that support core business operations. This role applies advanced full stack software, data, and AI engineering expertise to build internal platforms spanning field operations, pricing, safety and compliance, financial models, and structured data capture. The AI Software Developer operates with a high degree of autonomy, making architectural and technical decisions while ensuring solutions are reliable, measurable, secure, auditable, and aligned with enterprise standards.

 Responsibilities: 
 Designs and owns end to end systems, including data models, backend services, APIs, web applications, and mobile applications.
 Builds offline capable mobile and web applications for users working in remote environments with limited or no connectivity, including data synchronization, queuing, and conflict resolution.
 Develops applications supporting field operations, including labor time entry, production tracking, daily reporting, and equipment usage.
 Develops applications supporting pricing, proposal development, rate libraries, and historical pricing analysis.
 Develops applications supporting safety and compliance, including observations, hazard assessments, incident reporting, corrective actions, and training records.
 Develops financial models and planning applications, including budgeting, forecasting, profitability modeling, and period close workflows with versioning and audit history.
 Develops configurable data capture tools supporting photos, video, location, barcode scanning, and signatures.
 Establishes and maintains canonical data models for projects, cost structures, employees, equipment, customers, and vendors.
 Designs and owns AI solutions, including LLM based applications, classical machine learning models, and hybrid approaches.
 Builds and operates complex AI systems such as agentic workflows, retrieval augmented generation platforms, document extraction, anomaly detection, and natural language reporting.
 Evaluates ambiguous business problems and determines appropriate architectures, patterns, and modeling techniques.
 Defines and implements evaluation strategies, metrics, and feedback loops to measure model effectiveness and business impact.
 Leads the development of data pipelines, integrations, warehouse models, and evaluation datasets required to support enterprise systems.
 Integrates with enterprise systems including ERP, payroll, business intelligence, telematics, and collaboration platforms, and implements automated reconciliation and data integrity controls.
 Owns production readiness, including performance, reliability, cost, observability, and failure handling.
 Identifies and mitigates risks related to bias, hallucination, data leakage, and unintended AI behavior.
 Plans and executes system migrations, including data migration, parallel operation, validation, and rollback.
 Collaborates cross functionally with operations, project management, accounting, human resources, and safety to define requirements and guide solution design.
 Mentors and provides technical guidance to other team members.
 Contributes to the establishment and evolution of engineering standards, patterns, documentation, and best practices.

 Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
 Eight or more years of professional experience spanning software engineering, data engineering, machine learning engineering, or AI system development.
 Advanced full stack proficiency, including modern web frameworks, a production backend language such as Python, TypeScript, or C#, relational data modeling, SQL, APIs, testing, and system design.
 Demonstrated experience building offline first or local first applications, including synchronization and conflict resolution.
 Production mobile development experience on iOS and Android, including enterprise distribution and device management.
 Advanced proficiency in one or more large scale data platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, Amazon Redshift, Microsoft Fabric or Synapse, or similar.
 Strong applied knowledge of machine learning and artificial intelligence concepts, evaluation techniques, and failure modes.
 Hands on experience designing, building, and deploying LLM based systems using enterprise grade platforms and frameworks.
 Experience with one or more AI orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or similar.
 Deep understanding of data quality, feature relevance, and model behavior across structured and unstructured data.
 Experience building or integrating financial, planning, or forecasting models where accuracy, versioning, and auditability are required.
 Experience integrating with an ERP or comparable system of record.
 Experience deploying, monitoring, and iterating on systems in production environments.
 Working knowledge of enterprise security and access control, including single sign on, multifactor authentication, role based access, and handling of sensitive employee and business data.
 Ability to make and defend technical tradeoff decisions balancing accuracy, cost, risk, and scalability.
 Strong communication and leadership skills, with the ability to influence technical direction and mentor others.
 Experience in construction, utilities, field service, or manufacturing environments preferred.
 Bilingual English and Spanish preferred.

Looking for a place to grow your career and make a difference? RICK is the place for you! As a Principal Civil Project Engineer/Manager in Irvine, CA you will have an opportunity to work with a multi-disciplinary team on meaningful, landmark projects in the Irvine, CA area. As a RICK team member, you will help clients and communities turn their dreams into reality. You will learn from and work alongside industry-leading experts and together shape the future of tomorrow.
 Qualifications 
 Qualified candidate will have a BSCE degree, CA Registration as a Professional Civil Engineer, (or ability to obtain in next 6 months), plus a minimum of eight (8-12) years relevant experience; or the equivalent work experience of twelve (12-15) years in this industry.
 Candidates for this position must demonstrate:
 Independent thought and decision-making abilities
 Must demonstrate strong independent thought and decision-making abilities
 A minimum of three years management experience supervising the work of technical staff required
 Possess demonstrated leadership and supervisory skills
 Demonstrate Project management ability
 Be adept in establishing and maintaining strong and positive working relationships with clients/public-agency personnel and in-house staff
 Managerial experience will include the following:
 Management of construction documents and contracts
 Management of construction support and field coordination
 Management of project schedules and budgets
 Preparation of contracts, fee proposals, and scopes of work
 Significant experience in client and public-agency interactions
 Management of Design and Support Staff
 Technical experience will include the following:
 Ability to perform conceptual and preliminary engineering design studies (incorporating land use and zoning considerations, assessment and consideration of site constraints, infrastructure requirements, and potential regulatory issues)
 Preparation/processing of regulatory plans
 Preparation/processing of public improvement plans (private and public)
 Ability to perform constructability reviews
 Experience with a range of construction support services
 Knowledge of jurisdictional codes, standards, and procedures in the State of CA and the region is strongly preferred.
 AutoCAD/Civil 3D. CAD experience is required.
 Additional Skills: 
 Applies engineering principles, techniques, and procedures for Civil Engineering design
 Possesses working knowledge of business and management principles associated with strategic planning, resource allocation, leadership techniques, production procedures, interview and hiring methods and the coordination of people
 Accepts and carries out responsibility for the design team's direction, control and planning; sets realistic goals and makes decisions independently
 Exhibits a thorough understanding of jurisdictional processing
 Negotiates effectively
 Demonstrates a high level of leadership & management ability; accepts and responds appropriately to constructive feedback with others and applies seasoned time management
 Relates well and maintains a high level of respect and confidence from co-workers, public agencies
 Demonstrates a high level of competence in written and oral communication
 Possesses knowledge of CAD and its capabilities for preparing exhibits, studies and/or final plans
 What We Offer 
 Generous Benefits Package
 Medical, Dental, Vision, Profit Sharing, 401K, and Life and Disability Insurance and Personal Leave
 Holiday Parties, Team Building Activities and Events 
 Annual bonus potential
 At RICK you will find an abundance of opportunities for mentorship, growth, and (of course) fun! Learn more by visiting www.rickengineering.com
 RICK Engineering Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer 
 RICK employees are protected by laws designed to protect employees from discrimination based on race, religion, color, sex, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, parental status, national origin, age, disability, family medical history or genetic information, political affiliation, military service, or any other non-merit-based factor. These protections extend to all management practices and decisions, including recruitment and hiring practices, appraisal systems, promotions, and training and career development programs. RICK employees are also protected against retaliation if they engage in a protected activity, whistleblowing, or the exercise of any appeal or grievance right provided by law.
 Salary Range $130,000- $165,000
